| | |

_"Hello? Is this the Trump administration?
Yes, Americans would like their government open."_
**Yep, that's me, cowboy boots and all **– on Day 30 of President Trump and Republicans' government shutdown. You're probably wondering why I look like that.
[**So, friend, before I ask you to chip in toward my $30,000 mid-month goal ahead of the can't-miss deadline this Saturday,**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119239779/582402818/851209409?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1007-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5OWQ5ZDk5MC1lZGMwLWYwMTEtODE5Ni02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bssNbgX2CTZg7soKZTm4ikTCwA-O9-r1CDfa97hojcs=) allow me to explain:
See, long before any of this happened, I was a deciding vote to pass the Affordable Care Act – **because health care is a human right. **
That's why I and other Senate Democrats sounded the alarm for months about how the Affordable Care Act tax credits were set to expire in 2026. We _knew_ the GOP's failure to act would lead to health premiums **doubling, tripling or quadrupling** for roughly 225,000 working Coloradans and tens of millions more folks across the country, and we made sure they knew too.
So on Sept. 30, when their bill to fund the government still didn't include a plan to stop working families' premiums from skyrocketing, I voted NO, hoping that we would work out a bipartisan deal.
Fast-forward to Oct. 30 – _when this photo was taken_ – and the government was still shut down. Senate Republicans still refused to come to the table. Meanwhile:
* Around 900,000 federal employees were placed on furlough,
* About 2 million more federal employees, _and_ active-duty troops, were working without pay – as Speaker Mike Johnson extended the House’s **paid vacation** week after week,
* Airports across the country were facing mass delays,
* Regular folks were already seeing their premium estimates for 2026 go through the stratosphere, and
* Trump was _threatening to starve millions of kids_ until he got his way.

So on day 40 of the shutdown, I voted against the Republican bill to open the government.
Because I won't support a plan that failed to keep lifesaving health care in reach for so many people in Colorado.
**As the next governor of our state, I am committed to making health care more affordable. But to keep that promise, I first need your help to reach my $30,000 mid-month goal by midnight this Saturday.**

clean_body: This is why I'm running to bring my commitment to affordable health care back home as the next governor of our state. | | | = "Hello? Is this the Trump administration? Yes, Americans would like their government open." Yep, that's me, cowboy boots and all – on Day 30 of President Trump and Republicans' government shutdown. You're probably wondering why I look like that. = allow me to explain: See, long before any of this happened, I was a deciding vote to pass the Affordable Care Act – because health care is a human right. That's why I and other Senate Democrats sounded the alarm for months about how the Affordable Care Act tax credits were set to expire in 2026. We knew the GOP's failure to act would lead to health premiums doubling, tripling or quadrupling for roughly 225,000 working Coloradans and tens of millions more folks across the country, and we made sure they knew too. So on Sept. 30, when their bill to fund the government still didn't include a plan to stop working families' premiums from skyrocketing, I voted NO, hoping that we would work out a bipartisan deal. Fast-forward to Oct. 30 – when this photo was taken – and the government was still shut down. Senate Republicans still refused to come to the table. Meanwhile: Around 900,000 federal employees were placed on furlough, About 2 million more federal employees, and active-duty troops, were working without pay – as Speaker Mike Johnson extended the House’s paid vacation week after week, Airports across the country were facing mass delays, Regular folks were already seeing their premium estimates for 2026 go through the stratosphere, and Trump was threatening to starve millions of kids until he got his way. So on day 40 of the shutdown, I voted against the Republican bill to open the government. Because I won't support a plan that failed to keep lifesaving health care in reach for so many people in Colorado. As the next governor of our state, I am committed to making health care more affordable. ---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/lucaskunce/p/its-all-over-now?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

That was an... interesting... end to the shutdown.
Through the course of my Senate campaign I met hundreds of striking workers on strike lines in industries like retail, nursing, trucking, manufacturing, labor, and the building trades.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b1471f24-ef65-4288-a7d0-a2a95f8812ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Not a single one of them took the decision to strike lightly. Many of them were proud of what they made, the work they did, or the people they served. They were scared to go without pay while on the strike line or, even worse, scared that their employer would shut down their worksite and move away rather than negotiate.
But, even more compelling than fear was their desire to get a respectable share of the fruits of their labor, have long term security for their families, and live the American dream, a dream that shouldn't be reserved for just management and shareholders.
Frequently, the men and women I met on picket lines were striking because their employer had tried to double or triple their healthcare costs in the latest contract offer.
Sound familiar?
Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.GrCnsCYoNg1sxEOlKexEpKI0-9Ww99SowdVm8UZTif4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=178842499)
Supposedly, that's why certain Members of Congress were holding out on passing the budget year, causing the most recent government shutdown. They were, for all practical purposes, putting America on strike to secure healthcare subsidies for working Americans.
But there's one thing I learned from workers on the strike lines of Missouri that these Members of Congress apparently don't get: you don't go on strike unless you mean it, because a strike hurts. And I can tell you right now, when working people decide to put themselves, their coworkers, their families, and their community through a strike, they sure as hell aren't going to go without work for weeks or months only to settle for exactly what was offered to them on day one.
None of the striking workers I met ever failed to stand in solidarity and, because of that, eventually all of them got better than they were initially offered, in many cases, [historically more](https://substack.com/redirect/a25f869f-6cf0-4054-8137-b482e3b0a589?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
So if everyday people understand the concept that you don't go on strike unless you have the grit to see it through, why don't these Members of Congress get it?
Just like basically every worker has made it clear that they are not fond of strikes or the pain that come with them, I've made the point many times in the past that I am not a fan of government shutdowns. But you know what? People aren't stupid. We understand that sometimes fighting for something meaningful for yourself or others is going to hurt. But that it is the right decision if real gains are made.
On the flip side, we also understand that it's both ridiculous and embarrassing to initiate a painful fight you're not willing to see through to the end. What a waste.
In this case, the Members of Congress who put the country on strike and then decided to quit won absolutely nothing for putting everyone through it.
When Democrats asked me on the campaign trail why Democrats aren't liked, or why they are considered weak, this is a perfect example of why. The only thing people are going to remember from this whole ordeal is the confirming feeling that Democrats are spineless and don't stand and fight for anything.
The excuses they are giving are pathetic. Saying things like "the funding bill needed to pass as a 'clean' funding bill" and therefore it was wrong to demand the inclusion of healthcare subsidies.
Give me a break. Again, people aren't stupid and nobody is going to accept that.

The bill package was vast and included, as just one example among many, according to the [Senate Appropriations Committee's own Majority report](https://substack.com/redirect/2e0a4e00-2d72-4f53-b2a3-11f7c520d28b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), provisions as wide-flung as "Prevent[ing] the unregulated sale of intoxicating hemp-based or hemp-derived products, including Delta-8, from being sold online, in gas stations, and corner stores, while preserving non-intoxicating CBD and industrial hemp products."
They could toss in something as niche as preventing the unregulated sale of Delta-8, but voting for healthcare subsidies was not possible for the bill to remain "clean?"
Try selling an excuse like that as a reason to break solidarity for anyone who has ever walked a picket line.
No, really, I mean it. Try it.
Because that's exactly the swath of voters that has switched parties in recent years. And if they don't buy it, well, that will tell you something about how well it's going to sell.
Lucas

Peter,

Late last night, the House passed a bill to end the government shutdown.

I voted against it because this bill does absolutely nothing to address rising costs and the healthcare crisis that millions of American families now face.

This comes after Republicans spent nearly two months out of Washington and Congress – refusing to meet to work on a deal that includes extended healthcare subsidies and tackle the cost of living crisis.

Speaker Johnson is not taking a shred of accountability. The issues that Americans are struggling with are real, and with the passage of this bill, we are forced to trust that he will bring a vote on the ACA to the House floor.

This is the latest in a long string of examples why we must flip the House majority and move toward solutions – not let working families be used as partisan political pawns.

I’m going to keep fighting for you and do everything that I can to lower costs in CA-27. And as we look ahead to next year’s midterm elections, your ongoing support will be crucial to protecting this competitive seat and moving the needle toward a Democratic majority.

Donate >> https://secure.actblue.com/donate/gw-q4-2025?refcode=em-11.13.25-all-a

Thank you,

George

| **Dear Friend,** This Veterans Day hit home, reminding us of the bravery and sacrifice of those who defend our freedoms. From the beaches of Normandy to the mountains of Afghanistan, their courage defines what it means to be American. **Saluting these heroes isn’t just a tradition, it’s a reminder of the unbreakable spirit that built our nation.** As your representative, **I just cast a critical vote to reopen the government, fully fund our military, and protect Americans from political brinkmanship. No furloughs for our troops or VA workers, no wasting your tax dollars on games in Washington.** This bipartisan measure keeps offices running, strengthens national defense, and advances President Trump’s America First agenda, secure borders, strong defense, and economic opportunities for working families. **But the radical left hasn’t given up.** They are pouring millions from out-of-state billionaires and special interests into North Carolina to push open-border, weak-on-crime policies that threaten our communities. Silence is not an option. Your support helps us honor veterans, strengthen our borders with real enforcement and technology, and defend the North Carolina values we cherish: faith, family, freedom, and opportunity for all. **Together, we can fight back, mobilize voters, and hold the line against the Washington swamp.**

**(Clovis, CA)** \- Today, Supervisor Nathan Magsig announced he has received the endorsements of Senator Shannon Grove and Assemblywoman Alexandra Macedo for his campaign for State Senate. Senator Grove currently represents Senate District 12, and will be termed out of office in 2026.
Nathan Magsig released the following statement:_“It is an incredible honor to have Senator Shannon Grove’s endorsement. She has been a tireless fighter for our energy producers, our farmers, and for protecting California’s children. Shannon set a high bar for leadership in the Senate, standing up for our values and defending the industries that power and feed our State and Nation. Her legacy of courage, conviction, and service to the Central Valley will continue to inspire the next generation of conservative leaders.”_
Magsig continued, _“I’m also grateful to have the support of Alexandra Macedo, who in just one year has gained national attention for our Valley by standing up to waste and corruption in Sacramento. Her work in our community reflects the same commitment to faith, family, and freedom as so many of us. Together, we’ll continue fighting to ensure the voices of our Valley and our families are heard loud and clear in Sacramento.”_

This announcement follows Magsig’s growing support from Central Valley Leaders and members of the Senate and Assembly caucus, including:
Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, Assemblyman David Tangipa, State Senators: Rosilicie Ochoa Bogh, Steven Choi, Tony Strickland, and Kelly Seyarto, Kern County Sheriff Donny Youngblood, Bakersfield Councilman Larry Koman, Tehachapi City Manager Greg Garrett, Fresno County Supervisor Buddy Mendes, Fresno County Supervisor Garry Bredefeld, Tulare Supervisor Pete Vander Poel, Tulare Supervisor Dennis Townsend, Fresno County DA Lisa Smittcamp, Fresno County Sheriff John Zanoni, Fresno Mayor Jerry Dyer, and many more.

---
| | ###
Nathan Magsig is a current Fresno County Supervisor, former Mayor of Clovis, and is running for the 12th Senate District. His family, wife Julie and their three children, reside in Clovis, CA.

body:
We MUST stop this bill in the Senate and more like it but we need to unite and fight now, before opponents of voting rights in the Senate start checking voter suppression bills off their to-do list.
Why? Listen to Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut:
(Image of Richard Blumenthal speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_RB.jpg]
RUSH $25 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act, defend our right to vote, and stop opponents of voting rights from destroying our democracy >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=111325_3&amount=25]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
The Senate is standing up to stop the SAVE Act in its tracks, folks.
Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet:
(Image of Michael Bennet speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_MB.jpg]
Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come.
Please, Team, join these brave Senators today. Fuel our efforts to stop this dangerous legislation with $25 or whatever you can and ensure millions of women's voices continue to be heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=111325_3&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

We know the SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before the next election, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law.
If you missed it: This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point.
The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
The consequences of a bill like this passing would be simply catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $25 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=111325_3&amount=25]

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Peter, Republicans love to pretend their efforts to manipulate maps aren’t a direct attack on democracy. But even former Indiana Governor Mitch Daniels — a Republican — is speaking out against the state’s attempts to do Trump’s bidding by passing a mid-decade map redraw. All lawmakers would do well to listen to his warning that **attempts to gerrymander “come at the expense of public disgust; Hoosiers, like most Americans, place a high value on fairness and react badly to its naked violation.”** **This is an important reminder that Trump’s gerrymandering scheme — which allows politicians to pick their voters instead of voters picking their politicians — isn’t normal. And it isn’t how a democracy works.** The NDRC is the leading organization dedicated to protecting and defending fair maps nationwide. We’re fighting for fair representation by electing Democracy Defenders, combating ongoing gerrymandering, and making certain that Republican attempts to subvert the will of the people backfire on politicians who seek only to conserve their own power. **But we rely on grassroots donations from supporters like you to fuel this work now and into the future. clean_body: With anti-democracy forces doing everything they can to silence voters, we need a strong movement to fight back | Peter, Republicans love to pretend their efforts to manipulate maps aren’t a direct attack on democracy. But even former Indiana Governor Mitch Daniels — a Republican — is speaking out against the state’s attempts to do Trump’s bidding by passing a mid-decade map redraw. All lawmakers would do well to listen to his warning that attempts to gerrymander “come at the expense of public disgust; Hoosiers, like most Americans, place a high value on fairness and react badly to its naked violation.” This is an important reminder that Trump’s gerrymandering scheme — which allows politicians to pick their voters instead of voters picking their politicians — isn’t normal. And it isn’t how a democracy works. The NDRC is the leading organization dedicated to protecting and defending fair maps nationwide. We’re fighting for fair representation by electing Democracy Defenders, combating ongoing gerrymandering, and making certain that Republican attempts to subvert the will of the people backfire on politicians who seek only to conserve their own power. subject: Ending the shutdown isn’t enough
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott Peters for Congress
body:

| | Peter,

The good news is that the government is finally reopening. After the longest shutdown in our nation’s history, federal employees, service members, and families who were living in uncertainty can finally breathe a little easier.

But here’s the truth: ending the shutdown doesn’t mean the work is done. The deal that passed still fails to address the healthcare crisis that’s hitting families hard here in San Diego and across the country.

I voted no on this spending bill because it does nothing to stop healthcare premiums from skyrocketing. If we don’t act now, 28,000 people in our district alone could face higher costs next year. Families can’t wait any longer for relief.

I’m glad that air traffic controllers, TSA agents, and other federal employees will finally be compensated, and that food assistance programs can restart. But the same dysfunction that caused this shutdown is also keeping us from solving problems like the rising cost of healthcare.

That has to change. The American people deserve a Congress that works for them – one that can keep the government open and lower costs for working families.

[If you agree that healthcare must be part of the next budget deal, add your name to stand with me in calling for real action and accountability.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119241522/582436902/-838101234?refcode2=537b6418-f6c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&refcode=SP_EM_PT_180DO_251113_1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzdiNjQxOC1mNmMwLWYwMTEtODE5Ni02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6FsDi_4LFi0ROdC7MpNesswPswfga2JCV_f_VTRRJMk=&emci=d7efb811-f6c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=537b6418-f6c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=5258741) | **[ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119241523/582436903/-838101234?refcode2=537b6418-f6c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&refcode=SP_EM_PT_180DO_251113_1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzdiNjQxOC1mNmMwLWYwMTEtODE5Ni02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6FsDi_4LFi0ROdC7MpNesswPswfga2JCV_f_VTRRJMk=&emci=d7efb811-f6c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=537b6418-f6c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=5258741)**

After the longest shutdown in our nation’s history, federal employees, service members, and families who were living in uncertainty can finally breathe a little easier. But here’s the truth: ending the shutdown doesn’t mean the work is done. The deal that passed still fails to address the healthcare crisis that’s hitting families hard here in San Diego and across the country. I voted no on this spending bill because it does nothing to stop healthcare premiums from skyrocketing. If we don’t act now, 28,000 people in our district alone could face higher costs next year. Families can’t wait any longer for relief. | | I’m glad that air traffic controllers, TSA agents, and other federal employees will finally be compensated, and that food assistance programs can restart. #
Peter, it’s Chris Pappas. I want you to hear it from me first: **John Sununu just entered the race for U.S. Senate in New Hampshire.**
That’s right. This just became one of the toughest and most expensive races in the 2026 election. **[So before I go any further, I have to ask: Will you split $15 or more between my campaign and State Democrats Committee today?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/96920?refcode=em20251113-9710&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=9710%2E614464%2Ep1tgop)**

California’s future depends on investing in our families. That’s why Katie Porter is running for governor—the same-old status quo won’t cut it. We need to make sure families don’t just get by, but thrive.

As a public school parent and University of California professor, Katie knows that every dollar we invest in our kids pays dividends in the future, growing our economy and helping families thrive. That’s the kind of leadership California needs right now.

| Letter from the Chair
---
Shutdown Showdown Ended for now
Dear Nebraska Republicans,
We did it. After 43 grueling days, the government shutdown--engineered by Senate Democrats under Chuck Schumer's leadership--has ended. Funding is restored, federal workers are back on payroll, and essential services are resuming. This wasn't just a budget fight; it was a stark reminder of what happens when partisan spite overrides responsibility.
Schumer's strategy was clear: hold the entire nation hostage to block President Trump's border security priorities. But let's pause and ask the uncomfortable question: How long would Senator Schumer have let this drag on? Another week? A month? Until air traffic controllers walked off the job en masse, until national parks became permanent trash heaps, until Social Security checks stopped arriving for our seniors? And how much damage would he have allowed--billions in economic losses, shattered public trust, families unable to pay rent--before declaring "victory"?
The answer lies in the poison of spite. Schumer didn't just target Republicans; he targeted America. Spite is a fire that burns both ways. It scorched federal employees who missed paychecks, small businesses near shuttered parks, and travelers stranded by TSA chaos. But it also consumed Schumer's own party--exposing their willingness to weaponize government against citizens for political points. History will remember this not as leverage, but as self-inflicted sabotage.
Nebraska knows better. We balance budgets. We show up to work. We don't torch the barn to spite the mule. This shutdown's end is a win for pragmatism, for our state's values, and for the 800,000 workers who deserved better than being pawns in Schumer's game.
Stay vigilant. The fight for fiscal sanity and secure borders continues. Onward.
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

## Shutdown Ends, Stocks Tumble
President Trump [signed a funding bill Wednesday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdCB2MdxRuEhDd2lTIsMuhyNjI7yHdX8fESlfkGaa0bzRzNdjfFjnXXh-2o2NLHEMnJNnET7GtL6EYg4cKFl3xCnKYmfe_Yg1tiVACXok6_x71AWZhRm5KdjArWsA7qihWA1Tf-_1tDC1HbW6v3WT1a0l2xC3pPvCmYsGABqg1nVd2X4Cy8A9T22D907pmslJPKrv6IKsvPh3PPmo5rgV3qwie1LNh8JB4ZBzruYwzZepcLjQCgeAS1Dh8LySYeMg5d-8co2vxOUZhUs5XtterbL54jC0Z-e9S91N6fq5Wed_K-VfP50GfwIAAP__TiB82A) night to end the 43-day federal shutdown, the longest in U.S. history. The bill, passed 222-209 in the House, keeps the government running through January 2026 and restores pay for furloughed workers. Federal employees were ordered back to work on Thursday, including air traffic controllers, but the FAA warns that air travel [won't immediately return to normal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLEOnDAQRL_GdJy8i4G7wkUad5c2JdrD68ORsRHeO8TfR0TKF6SZajRv9H49pyfFFPP7J61sJZQp81ETi_A-1eUjvhyZs68U9_IqEmjmLU2osW8BWjCTp5jOyTTeBmbkrmEL49AB3NFAs1jfhz4EGvthoAe-DPIYSHsTwDwGc5-baK81ADAA2mh9o8cLiIEf_Oo7vA_KaPZRyn77XWKWhUM6y5f321zWJtlFZKuq-6HQKXTHcdw-laR4Oq-CQlel7KdCJzt9OSl0F0-hA7iiU-hCiu9FWs-JztrOlGdOiSSWXNv3hcorZ2n_-Wg_myfhqtDdRzRao9Z6VOia3frtiCnFOozK6PdKMf29Kf_l9mvxTwAAAP__nOuNOw). For now it's keeping total flight reductions at 6%. The end of the shutdown added to economic uncertainty, as officials warned that some key data, such as October's unemployment rate, may never be released. Market odds of a December rate cut have dropped sharply from 95% to around 50%. [Stocks took a dive Thursday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ymzAQhZ8GumW0QoBdUKShu2lTMgtarhTrh0hrM377jPMK6c-cc77v19f6RT749P2TIs9y5DXxVQOLcFmre4rNV-JkK_mStywH7XyGVSs9ACKgWS358F5Na-eDWXPf8ozT2CPetMHWzbyP_c3aOx_KjNPEg1GoepxGqyfah63186cNEQ2iMkp1dN-QGPnO29Dr29gYxdZLLt3v7JM4PsI7v7h0e45tmJ3IWZv-R6OXRi-HT5R27t7kcv4kGr18kBq9BP_iRi9V8v6ASOXBApItvcHmC-QZt8AVbkrB-dmpcHlxkKha-gP1hEEpcBQjF7ZAFXx6cZVcKpxUGAoJw_4U2FgqaFTYj_fJdE5iaMtsz8uH4Os4NUZ9R_Lh33_5L-mvWf8NAAD__-H-l-w), with the Dow falling nearly 800 points and the Nasdaq losing over 2%, as investors pulled back amid new doubts the Fed will cut interest rates next month.
## DOJ Sues California Over Redistricting
The U.S. Justice Department filed suit Thursday [against California Gov. Gavin Newsom](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OtCAUxZ9GO4wXmRELiq-xm6_d0iBcxjtBMIBD5u03br3dtuck58_v67E8NHkKz_96R1VcXALW7LEUTEvezmJjDRhs1pTiGovTBg-_8J7fGAADsVhN_rOI1iqHyHFoUcF4HwAkF9BuSvBRODNK5DgON2mhnziXg3VynZyUriV1pQGAAOhF33d6WkEj4ITrbeDy3ogeLZWYulekUDZ0_hPfmDoT99arrZQjN8O_hs8Nn2utXVjN9eLyGz4f0VMhkxs-v85cyCCzeOhUdgzlV5FdPZl5XfNJhRntycUUSGeW0CZdA9vimZHt-mDJBM3FMI7QJmWPSt5Tvo-N6J-7Jv8zsvyJ7Fvx7wAAAP__scCQ5w) and Secretary of State Shirley Weber, claiming the state's new redistricting plan under Proposition 50 violates the Constitution. The federal government says the plan, approved by voters, creates [racially gerrymandered congressional districts](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO5CAQRU-DM1oUxu7ugGATZ7PphlZhinatMFhQntbcfjVzhY3_13vS-_OxfiBnLq_feJCXVNdC755JhNra90tifRcqsSO3Gqok3OjMqzV20gAa3BqR89fqhugTkaVxIA_3eQR4WAfD7ulxnwJuMd1jNMmNczAQNjTTY3tCoHFg_00DAAdgnDE3fAZAAnpSmEb7mJUzFFlqu_2tXGSnlL_qJ7XbVo8h-13k7Gr8peyi7CI77Zzz96bs0uh1ZRSuRdllq1cTHVAkU1d2mWbjZme0tOs4NcaDC3dpP3ed-LVL1xtmTrUVRn3gqewyNB_PN-fMfb4rZ14H8o9tkP_K9-ntvwAAAP__-CCGbQ) that prioritize Latino demographics, breaching the Equal Protection Clause. Attorney General Pam Bondi [called it a "brazen power grab,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2upSAUxfGnwQ4jiF8FxTR2d9opzVY2um8QDOyjOW8_OZN5g1uv5J-V35-v5QsoUNx_w4mWfVoiPiUgM-alHC926YkYXQHKaU3sYcMrLLrRnVRKKrM4oPBeTOWsR9TYVmjV0LdKjdqo6rDN2nkDplu7aUDdu6HbpmEaBt-PCrvRV2Q_NaWUUaoxTVPDtCpAhROuXavHXpgGHXHK9XeiyAf68E435npLZxXswXwV0f4SehZ6fp6n_n4Vpg3rPd1Cz-kCoecrCz3_H6TDCzKfGFmWFxa5f3IxZbnDTVF-CNIpNwjkU44ERWbYUK5Q0MmMjgpn2pjiLq8AscrWXQ-FQKUfhGn2Eyj8e8c_Ir2t_hsAAP__1yKO_w)" aiming to lock in one-party control. The case is pending in federal court in Los Angeles.

body:
Friends– The longest government shutdown in American history is coming to an end, but that doesn’t mean that Virginians are out of danger.
| | |

| Friends-
The longest government shutdown in American history is coming to an end, but that doesn't mean that Virginians are out of danger. Congress's failure to renew expiring Affordable Care Act tax credits puts [350,000 Virginians](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001iCoyCQB2widj9awBuz4fJBwwsNHNGXjLo0b4WfNFrBvs_BVt7tb-ukmJKhAloIoIwH-kmBiZFQVGzYIUzel9KUUz6J_FlHuX9UDm-hNDw53DnnRUkghRV9uQKqyY_ZM33fVS9n_ei-IWlU7n0BGhPxuAex9rIhkPIDcFRXmPcukNP_JGgqlpMuDdSX3pjMAAAG6gTlRjME26iHNzvJAhpDPbTKWyWnxHhUf8zJtqTVfsBgEP1Va83fCwaqTLeusVF8vkvFe5Gv3706ZpLTG6Zw16jzrJA0Se65egvJy7wQE=&c=hfsFB38IE30Zy4Exep9gp_sOqMSCRoiXGfYlefq6j4bQLu7DUKc0kA==&ch=6mQeQ3FR16Fj5JTWkiCzw_Ohx4cxLidmlG5WDlkwYGUxxfNyzDxlQw==) at risk of losing access to healthcare coverage, and unless the federal government acts by the end of the year, 411,000 Virginians will see higher insurance rates.

## Lawmakers Discuss Campus Speech
Texas House and Senate members of the newly formed Select Committee on Civil Discourse and Freedom of Speech met for the first time yesterday, engaging in a prolonged discussion about [speech on college campuses](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGu3CAQRb8Gd6yYWQxL4SKNu5c2pTULYxsFLxaw67d_H_klyg-8bnRHutI599fH9EExxcfykzYe2uecpwcfNXFrXKa5MNed2a8rU4mP5U7vlAuFCRX2EkCCngLF9J50F4a7Cg46HsCaKyBYpbp16J0JBmcy7MD3Boy7sWOr2d4tKe-7OJxlAKABFWh1ufU88804hxyuPrDQikNsuVzayo0_qc7pnV9cLj5vXRrW1vYqrj8EjgLH4zguv19PPp8CRyot-sQCx5NL4LjnFFv05_nVJRMvsSZqz8L_szU_K8vKD2osfd622BqzPH3Iv0LkPVLlKn1OiReWnrb9eQZzLLXJf74EjmicnI11AayVBNBLHdBJumqQPhCh8SogqK4MYT9iSrEaK7RaNorpi7B9b5fXgH8CAAD__zoYo2A) with university officials, students, and representatives from the attorney general’s office and Turning Point USA. The committee was formed following the assassination of outspoken Christian and conservative activist Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University in September. Students at Texas Tech and Texas State [were expelled](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuunTAYhFcDnZEfHB6FizR0N21K9GMPYB2Dke0Ll91HnCwh9Tw03_z5Gr_Iebcvv2mDzj9zGHdcySNnxHGOQDoAs66g6PZlotuHSHaUXL6YEEzUoyXn77EurZ647UUJLdpGCSlazstVT4ZUN5NSU9u-bN8r1aExhhsLdG3XlU4_ZUKIWkgual51L8zomr6XsMpYFDWHdTnEKq_I-KE0-zuciJUJW-n1mvORCvWrkEMhh-u6qndczkcs5PDQFHL4xJina6M3YmKJbmaC91iQ2EonWA5sIk-7AXuw2T9udrm8Mvud78fwBg5mXTLhOyYw407ny6jtcTnvXWraoubLRs5_luX_-_PU8m8AAAD__xTKjjo) for celebrating Kirk’s death, and the University of North Texas was investigated for its response to students who reportedly expressed approval of his murder. University of Austin President Jim Davis said he aims to create a culture of compassion and respect while maintaining a [steadfast commitment to free speech](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAURp8GbzcC_BcPDF28pWtHC8PFoGITwY2dvH3ltG_Q-ZOOvnO-btNNhxi25VOvqOjp0rThUSISYZ5cRix3ROM96hy2ZdavmLK2k-SyBSFANJPVIb6mprJq5nYQFSrRd7WQoue88so13dxyaYx11hp0thMtH3RfcylqN7gqqBMmhGiE5KLhl2uLDq_dMEi0tbHIGo42UMoX8kj41MXFV9oxX0xaq6g80b2w-oPJkcnRzEU_CoXtXJkcTx0mx5iMjkyOB4LXOwIlWJAgEOSweII3F6I-Vv2NuYBPheDPGtIGZwr4bQGa4LGFHXMJFLBUWdn7EWIMpetZw5dVh_j-Rv8ruiv5EwAA__8DpY6z). Although he vowed to protect offensive or even hateful speech, he insisted the "heckler's veto" would not be tolerated. "_We do not want hateful, ugly ideas, but we also respect the First Amendment's protection of ideas, and when they cross over into conduct or illegal or unprotected speech, we are very careful about that_ ," [he said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL_upCAUhZ8GOwwX8F9BsY3dbLulQbkq8SoG2HF8-42zj_BrTnOSL-c7f17Dy3ryx_Lb7mjyZw7DgVcizBnjMEfEdCJO64o2-mMZ7U0hWjdIISsOwEEPznq6B104MwrXQYEGmlqBhEaIYjXNPFZV1UKH4zi6WkOjpALVqlEpnKwovHlgAKBBCtCibCucsa27TqJTk0OmBTqfQyzzihk_Ns10hzfGcgp7QWbN-UxM_WKyZ7K_rqvcKL-fksn-YTPZAzyhmey_AE722u2GMfHHjGdM2e_huPlk9_Nv4v-t-RyIwuWPhTu0eeXTaiN55JuPG5N9EY07L0_kU90wLZbdevquyj_78m3kvwAAAP__RYmJVA).
## 21 Arlington Gang Members Arrested
The Arlington Police Department announced the [arrests of 21 alleged members](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdCDv4pBQuPgbuvztlWjxrsE6B0e2FZK3P3GvcN0Uoxl939d9vlOIYV__00Nsffs073KUKLVKnn0WKU8Rt21COezrQp-YMvGMGi8tQAtmZgrxM5uG7aJ5hEYsXIceEK5aN5vtx9tgQHvPnolxweHinGDP7AFxdE2w5xgAGEANRne3i3i5DeOIwr1jUUYLh5pyVzep8qbi4ye9JHcuPZpot1qfRfX_FE4Kp-M4Op_e5sQ4CwqnMyqcKJ-gNe2tX0L7HZzjJO1K-9pSzlJqabLl5xFiDGW4KqPXB4X4-1L_5uZl8ScAAP__24h6pA) of the local Kiccdoe gang on Wednesday, accusing the group of 180 violent crimes since January 2022. name: Amy Carnevale
subject: CONVENTION 2026: What you need to know right now
body:
Save the date: April 25, 2026
| | | | | [](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0014hBJHy-EZbWH2_tydRr-4zQfFV3FKOe2IyOhz-RSeoRZEvtwAeGgSMhCvB7SvC1xowwMNvca6mT_9aEUvsHqage1qpenkM6SEtpUGEogqqXmwRAcMo1yYMC791BRK7TCVrFd_KFf4dz93wiygGB3Jw==&c=WGWILL36BzvBT1L9hX0rxx-VA1wpshByNQhrGfJvcqKIvnf5wNXdMA==&ch=2aGjmlysutB4Rt64Yc77e72xxb_gB1AHcZW7VmMr0xlsW1mQHGmxDQ==)
---
| Dear Peter,
Planning for next April's Convention is in full swing. Here's what you need to know right now:
* Convention will be held on Saturday, April 25, 2026 at the DCU Center in Worcester. Held every four years, it remains the largest gathering of Republican activists in Massachusetts.

* While the Republican State Committee is still finalizing the 2026 rules, one thing is already confirmed: we have room for more than 5,500 delegates, and preparations are underway to maximize the number of credentialed delegates attending the convention.

* Given the hotly contested state-wide races, interest in this convention is already running high.

* Convention Eve continues to be one of the most enjoyable traditions, with campaigns and organizations hosting a variety of events throughout the host city.

* Delegates can expect to hear from notable national figures, as well as the full slate of statewide candidates. Our nominating convention celebrates who we are as a party.

* To participate as a delegate, individuals must be registered Republicans by December 31, 2025.

* To qualify to nominate delegates, Republican Ward & Town Committees must be organized by December 31, 2025. Final delegate numbers are still being determined.

Our team at the MassGOP is bursting with excitement at the prospect of hosting a successful and fun event in April aimed at winning back the corner office, building our seats in the legislature and re-establishing a Republican presence at the federal level.
A dedicated convention portal will be launching on our website soon with additional details and resources.
Stay tuned!
Best,
---
| |
---
| Amy Carnevale Chair, Massachusetts Republican Party

| | Fellow Conservative,Elon Musk is right. It isn’t rocket-science. It’s basic math. It’s also a ticking time-bomb set by Joe Biden and Kamala Harris – in the form of 11.5 million illegals entering our country on their watch – one which will explode shortly after President Trump leaves office in 2029.While you and I have no doubt President Trump will deliver on his promise to secure the border, this threat will not go away. The truth is, without immediate action, these illegal aliens will be counted in the U.S. Census, which determines both the apportionment of seats in the House of Representatives _and_ the number of electoral votes given to each state. Whether they came because, four years ago, Kamala Harris and Joe Biden prompted them to “surge to the border” for asylum or because of blue-states offering sanctuary status, “free” health care, “free” cell phones, “free” housing, and “free” college...it doesn’t matter. The result is the same.Your vote is _already_ being **watered down** in Congress. Your vote is _already_ being **watered down** in the Electoral College.And every day reports are popping up of non-citizens, illegal aliens, and convicted felons being registered to vote in cities and entire swing-states across the country, which means your vote may be fully **canceled out in future elections**. **_American elections should be decided by American citizens._****[If you agree then please sign your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution so the chaos we’re seeing now _never_ happens again in America.](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zcdaejplc3an9nlbbftvkao1kdtvsa4nof21jlk8_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgm8ob6cth2bs)**Because, here’s the scary part:The last census took place in 2020. That was _before_ the 11.5 million illegal aliens who invaded our country under Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. To put it in context, there are only 8 states in America with a population over 11 million. So, it’s as if the radical Left just imported the 9th largest state in America. That’s more than North Carolina (10.8 million), Michigan (10 million), New Jersey (9.2 million), or Virginia (8.7 million).You get the picture. That’s why urgent action is needed to pass a Constitutional Amendment to ban illegal aliens from voting and from being counted for purposes of congressional and electoral vote apportionment. The next census in less than 6 years away. If those 11.5 million illegal aliens are counted in the census or are allowed to vote in the intervening years, you and I simply won’t have a country. **[It’s vitally important that your representatives in Washington and in your state legislature hear this demand directly from you.](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zesagc2v478staslclvfk57l7v0hg3o3uk1emolg_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgm8ob6cth2bs)** Because, quite honestly, they think they can pull a fast one on you. They think you and I will be so relieved to see the border secure again and criminal illegal aliens deported, that you and I will be oblivious to this threat lying dormant under our very eyes.No way.My name is Rebecca Weber. I’m the chairwoman of AMAC Action. **AMAC Action is the most influential advocacy group in the country when it comes to standing for the values of conservative Seniors.****We’ve got 72 chapters and 300 volunteer delegates, who are the “feet on the street” advocates who contact Members of Congress and state legislators in their district offices.** **Moreover, our chapters and delegates help organize Town Hall meetings with elected officials and candidates to enable those locally of our 2,000,000 AMAC members to meet, hear, and question them.****And you should also know that we now have more than 337,000 AMAC members who respond to our “calls-to-action” and weigh in with members of the** **U.S. House and Senate, as well as their state legislators on the issues.** Quite simply, when we speak, Washington listens. [](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zgl89732v826qrch1kbfi150n2sv8ln1d4k41lbg_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgm8ob6cth2bs)**[And AMAC Action needs your help today in this do-or-die battle to pass a Constitutional Amendment to protect your vote from being canceled out by an illegal alien or a convicted felon.](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zlg7riam3vsg1v0tjuprldolqvs3di4i6fqvn3i0_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgm8ob6cth2bs)** But I can’t do it without you. **No matter what issue you care about the most, if you and I don’t have a secure,_honest_ elections... none of it matters.**Inflation. Illegal immigration. Violent Crime. Drug use. Homelessness. The 2nd Amendment. Out of control spending. Social Security and Medicare insolvency. Right to Life. Indoctrination in our schools. Endless foreign wars. You name it. **[So please follow this link to sign your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zqihrblgo47jr2qmhas13q6c6sb8r0quuhrdac48_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgm8ob6cth2bs)** so that AMAC Action can put your representatives in Washington and in the state legislature on notice with a simple demand: Namely, that you will not tolerate this erosion of your vote.Now, here’s the bad news:Most state constitutions grant voting rights to “every” citizen, open-ended language that liberal activists argue permits localities to authorize non-citizen and even illegal alien voting. States should amend their constitutions to instead permit “only” citizens to vote. But there’s good news, too:Seven states have _expressly_ banned non-citizen voting already: Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Louisiana, North Dakota, and Ohio.**What’s more, voters approve of constitutional amendments to ban non-citizen voting by overwhelming margins. Nearly 77% of Ohio voters approved a measure in 2022, while nearly 63% of Colorado voters approved one in 2020.** This is a solution whose time has come. You and I can do this. **[That’s why, when you’ve signed your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zvcp3b01d36h3toefhfp81avtq46croq7rh9b7m8_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgm8ob6cth2bs), I'm also asking you to make a one-time contribution of $35 to give AMAC Action the resources to send out, collect, process, and tabulate millions of petitions.** The reality is, we don’t get a dime of taxpayer funding. Our funding comes from grassroots conservatives like you who care deeply about the future of America. This is important. _It means we can’t be bought._ On the other hand, the leftwing election fraud machine is funded by leftwing billionaires like Mark Zuckerberg and George Soros who are actively funneling _billions_ to dark money “non-profit” groups to “**reshape** ” our elections and our electorate.With that said, if you’re able to make a larger contribution – say $50, $75, $125, $250, $500, or even $1,000 – it would really be a life saver. Please hurry. In order to secure your vote in all future elections – and with 11.5 million illegals chomping to be included in the next census – **[your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution is vitally important.](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zeg2jc3ilnti4ojfsb5fhaob349sef269to3pd80_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgm8ob6cth2bs)** Yes, this is about saving your vote from being canceled. It’s also about saving America.And it all starts with the straightforward premise that non-citizens and illegal aliens – no matter how many Kamala Harris and Joe Biden imported on their watch – should be banned from voting _and_ banned from being counted for apportioning congressional seats and electoral votes. Thank you in advance for joining the fight to secure your vote

Whether they came because, four years ago, Kamala Harris and Joe Biden prompted them to “surge to the border” for asylum or because of blue-states offering sanctuary status, “free” health care, “free” cell phones, “free” housing, and “free” college...it doesn’t matter. The result is the same.Your vote is already being watered down in Congress. Your vote is already being watered down in the Electoral College.And every day reports are popping up of non-citizens, illegal aliens, and convicted felons being registered to vote in cities and entire swing-states across the country, which means your vote may be fully canceled out in future elections. American elections should be decided by American citizens., here’s the scary part:The last census took place in 2020. That was before the 11.5 million illegal aliens who invaded our country under Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. To put it in context, there are only 8 states in America with a population over 11 million. So, it’s as if the radical Left just imported the 9th largest state in America. That’s more than North Carolina (10.8 million), Michigan (10 million), New Jersey (9.2 million), or Virginia (8.7 million).You get the picture. That’s why urgent action is needed to pass a Constitutional Amendment to ban illegal aliens from voting and from being counted for purposes of congressional and electoral vote apportionment. The next census in less than 6 years away. If those 11.5 million illegal aliens are counted in the census or are allowed to vote in the intervening years, you and I simply won’t have a country. Because, quite honestly, they think they can pull a fast one on you. They think you and I will be so relieved to see the border secure again and criminal illegal aliens deported, that you and I will be oblivious to this threat lying dormant under our very eyes.No way.My name is Rebecca Weber. I’m the chairwoman of AMAC Action. AMAC Action is the most influential advocacy group in the country when it comes to standing for the values of conservative Seniors.We’ve got 72 chapters and 300 volunteer delegates, who are the “feet on the street” advocates who contact Members of Congress and state legislators in their district offices. Moreover, our chapters and delegates help organize Town Hall meetings with elected officials and candidates to enable those locally of our 2,000,000 AMAC members to meet, hear, and question them.And you should also know that we now have more than 337,000 AMAC members who respond to our “calls-to-action” and weigh in with members of the U.S. House and Senate, as well as their state legislators on the issues. Quite simply, when we speak, Washington listens. But I can’t do it without you. No matter what issue you care about the most, if you and I don’t have a secure,honest elections... none of it matters.Inflation. Illegal immigration. Violent Crime. Drug use. Homelessness. The 2nd Amendment. Out of control spending. Social Security and Medicare insolvency. Right to Life. Indoctrination in our schools. Endless foreign wars. You name it. so that AMAC Action can put your representatives in Washington and in the state legislature on notice with a simple demand: Namely, that you will not tolerate this erosion of your vote.Now, here’s the bad news:Most state constitutions grant voting rights to “every” citizen, open-ended language that liberal activists argue permits localities to authorize non-citizen and even illegal alien voting. States should amend their constitutions to instead permit “only” citizens to vote. But there’s good news, too:Seven states have expressly banned non-citizen voting already: Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Louisiana, North Dakota, and Ohio.What’s more, voters approve of constitutional amendments to ban non-citizen voting by overwhelming margins. Nearly 77% of Ohio voters approved a measure in 2022, while nearly 63% of Colorado voters approved one in 2020. This is a solution whose time has come. You and I can do this. , I'm also asking you to make a one-time contribution of $35 to give AMAC Action the resources to send out, collect, process, and tabulate millions of petitions. The reality is, we don’t get a dime of taxpayer funding. Our funding comes from grassroots conservatives like you who care deeply about the future of America. This is important. It means we can’t be bought. On the other hand, the leftwing election fraud machine is funded by leftwing billionaires like Mark Zuckerberg and George Soros who are actively funneling billions to dark money “non-profit” groups to “reshape ” our elections and our electorate.With that said, if you’re able to make a larger contribution – say $50, $75, $125, $250, $500, or even $1,000 – it would really be a life saver. [But today, I have to at least break my silence because I just received information that will UPEND the 2026 elections. ](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zt1q7496d75qpohsqe4l1pgm02h3eccffrtjs3io_rp22sh2s8i6eor6chgmao32c1h2bs)

And this new poll shows us our clear path to victory.

name: Pat Harrigan
subject: I've seen what bad leadership costs on the battlefield
disclaimer_text: Paid for by The Pat Harrigan Committee
body:
Your signature is missing from our petition to hold the Democrats accountable

|

I hope you'll take a moment to read this, Friend - because we're facing a crossroads, and I refuse to stand silently while the future we've promised our country slips away.

From the minute I decided to run for Congress here in North Carolina, I promised myself and my district one thing: **I will always put people first.** Not politics. Not appearances. Not vague promises that sound nice but deliver nothing. Real results for real people.

Here's the hard truth: we're seeing important issues being ignored. Priorities are being misplaced. Democrat leaders who claim to be the 'party of compassion' held our country hostage to appease the far-left fringe.

Their leadership isn't even hiding it anymore; just listen to the second most powerful Democrat in Congress, Katherine Clark, who said this:

_**" Shutdowns are terrible, and of course, there will be families that are going to suffer, but it is one of the few leverage times we have."**_

YES, she actually said that!

They said the quiet part out loud; they saw our service members, air traffic controllers, and working-class Americans as pawns in a political chess game. That's not just wrong, it's disgusting.

I've seen what bad leadership costs on the battlefield, and I know what weak, self-serving leadership costs our country today.

It's time to stop using Americans as leverage, hit the ground running, and start putting the country first, NOT party politics.

I know you’re busy, so I’ll keep this quick.
I'm sharing **three reasons to chip in** to help me keep Michigan blue and flip the Senate. But if you’re already fired up and ready to go, **[you can give right here:](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/8691?t=4&akid=1352%2E49239%2E1ir3b7)**

**1\. I was born and raised in Michigan.** My parents ran a small landscaping business, and some of my earliest memories are helping them while covered in grease and grime. **I’m not the flashiest candidate – I’m a car geek who gets jazzed about manufacturing.** But I’ve spent my career delivering real results, not trying to go viral.
**2\. I helped save 200,000 Michigan jobs under President Obama.** When the auto industry was on the brink during the 2008 recession, we worked our tails off to bring workers, unions, and companies together – and we pulled Michigan’s economy back from the edge.
**3\. I’ve built a coalition that can win.** I’m strong with independent voters, endorsed by labor, and trusted by faith leaders and local officials. **And the polls show it:****I’m the best Democrat to beat MAGA Mike Rogers.**
If you believe Michigan deserves a senator who knows this state, loves it, and has a track record of fighting for working families, I’m your gal, null.

---
Hi Peter,

Her Bold Move has supported hundreds of women across the country, including me. And today, I am proud to join them in officially endorsing Aftyn Behn as we near her General Election (a Special Election) for Tennessee's 7th Congressional District on **December 2nd.**

Last month, Aftyn Behn won her primary election. She was the only woman running in the primary and the only real champion for the women of Tennessee. I'm writing to you today, with the help of Her Bold Move, because this is by no means a typical race, and Aftyn isn’t a typical candidate.

[**Before I share more, Aftyn’s election is only a few weeks away. Will you chip in a split contribution of $20.25 or more today and join me + Her Bold Move in supporting Aftyn Behn for Congress?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hbm-aftyn/?refcode=EM_F_251106AllieB_N_AP_NO_10_G_N_L1&amount=20.25)

I know firsthand what happens when men in power pass laws that strip women of the right to control their own health. When my pregnancy developed fatal complications, Tennessee’s abortion ban would’ve forced me to carry until my life was in danger, so I had no choice but to flee the state. Speaking out became necessary, and I told my story in front of the state Capitol, in Congress, and to anyone who would listen—because silence never protected anyone.

**And every step of the way, Aftyn Behn was there.** Long before she ran for office herself, Aftyn was organizing alongside women like me, pushing back on Tennessee’s abortion ban, and amplifying the voices of those harmed by it. In the state legislature, she didn’t just vote the right way—she fought publicly and unapologetically against Republican attempts to criminalize healthcare, control our bodies, and punish families in crisis. When others looked away, she leaned in. When they tried to silence us, she gave us a microphone.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119265929/582495885/-1821248200?refcode=EM_F_251106AllieB_N_AP_NO_10_G_N_P1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImUzOWMyZDYzLTY2YzEtZjAxMS04MTk2LTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=tNOMq8KBGWPQuW0ubia3dsfitBCClFH8Qq_ZzTGMgYQ=)
---
_Pictured: Rep. Aftyn Behn, D-Nashville, stands at her desk during a legislative session Tuesday, April 23, 2024, when the Underage Abortion Trafficking Act, a law criminalizing adults who "intentionally recruit, harbor, or transport" an unemancipated minor to get an abortion without notarized parental consent, passed in the majority-male TN legislature 74-24. Behn filed suit against the law._
---
That’s why I believe so deeply in Aftyn’s campaign for Congress. She has proven, time and again, that she will never back down when it comes to protecting our fundamental rights. She knows these fights aren’t abstract policy debates—they are life-and-death struggles for women, mothers, and families across Tennessee.

This race is about more than politics. It is about whether women’s lives and freedoms will continue to be treated as negotiable. Tennessee took my choice away when I needed it most, but I chose to fight back. **And today, I am choosing to fight alongside Aftyn Behn, because she has been in this fight from the very beginning.**

[**Will you join me in this fight by pitching in a split $20.25 or more contribution between Aftyn Behn’s campaign and Her Bold Move, the incredible organization that has been helping women like us, today?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hbm-aftyn/?refcode=EM_F_251106AllieB_N_AP_NO_10_G_N_L2&amount=20.25)

And today, I am proud to join them in officially endorsing Aftyn Behn as we near her General Election (a Special Election) for Tennessee's 7th Congressional District on December 2nd. Last month, Aftyn Behn won her primary election. She was the only woman running in the primary and the only real champion for the women of Tennessee. I'm writing to you today, with the help of Her Bold Move, because this is by no means a typical race, and Aftyn isn’t a typical candidate. I know firsthand what happens when men in power pass laws that strip women of the right to control their own health. When my pregnancy developed fatal complications, Tennessee’s abortion ban would’ve forced me to carry until my life was in danger, so I had no choice but to flee the state. Speaking out became necessary, and I told my story in front of the state Capitol, in Congress, and to anyone who would listen—because silence never protected anyone. And every step of the way, Aftyn Behn was there. Long before she ran for office herself, Aftyn was organizing alongside women like me, pushing back on Tennessee’s abortion ban, and amplifying the voices of those harmed by it. In the state legislature, she didn’t just vote the right way—she fought publicly and unapologetically against Republican attempts to criminalize healthcare, control our bodies, and punish families in crisis. When others looked away, she leaned in. When they tried to silence us, she gave us a microphone. = Pictured: Rep. Aftyn Behn, D-Nashville, stands at her desk during a legislative session Tuesday, April 23, 2024, when the Underage Abortion Trafficking Act, a law criminalizing adults who "intentionally recruit, harbor, or transport" an unemancipated minor to get an abortion without notarized parental consent, passed in the majority-male TN legislature 74-24. Behn filed suit against the law. That’s why I believe so deeply in Aftyn’s campaign for Congress. And today, I am choosing to fight alongside Aftyn Behn, because she has been in this fight from the very beginning. #
Peter —
With our mid-quarter deadline approaching at midnight tomorrow, we’re lowering our ask to $2.
Yes, just $2.
We know not everybody can chip in $20, $10, or even $5. But we’re hoping that by lowering our ask to $2, more people might be able to chip in to help VoteVets hit our goals ahead of tomorrow’s deadline.
So, yes. $2 because Donald Trump is destroying the United States Military.
$2 because millions of Veterans are losing access to health care.
$2 because millions more people, including countless military families, are about to see the prices of their health insurance skyrocket.
And yes, $2 for VoteVets because we are one of the only organizations in the country doing anything about it.
**[If any of that seems worth a donation of $2, we’re respectfully asking you to chip in. name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: From the Front with Patrick J. Murphy: Engaging the Conversation and the Community
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
Hi Friends,
It’s been another full and meaningful week talking about our most important issues. Here’s a look at what I covered.
In the Media: Elevating the National Conversation
This week was a full-on media blitz. I appeared on two Fox News segments and spoke virtually with London’s GB News, all in the same day.
On Wednesday, I joined Fox Business Digital for a conversation about the Democrats’ big wins in last week’s elections and what it says about the direction of our country in this moment.
Later that afternoon, I went on The Story with Martha MacCallum , and spoke about how the White House’s 50-year mortgage proposal ($400K home would cost $1.2 million) is not the answer for Americans seeking the dream of affordable homeownership. It’s only going to increase the price homeowners pay over time, leading to more debt. We also discussed the MAGA reaction to President Trump’s comments on H-1B visas and tonight’s White House dinner with business leaders.
https://www.mediamatters.org/fox-news/fox-news-guest-noah-rothman-says-trumps-50-year-mortgage-plan-one-those-ideas-you-have [https://www.mediamatters.org/fox-news/fox-news-guest-noah-rothman-says-trumps-50-year-mortgage-plan-one-those-ideas-you-have]
Later that day, I joined GB News for the first time to discuss reports that the UK suspended intelligence sharing with the US over recent drug-boat strikes. I made clear that any use of force by the United States must be grounded in constitutional authority and respect for international law. Without congressional authorization, it’s a breach of both our norms and global expectations. We must hold ourselves to the standard laid out in our laws and US Constitution.
https://www.youtube.com/live/JPShN0rioUE?si=BdI0b-NovWlBBn9B [https://www.youtube.com/live/JPShN0rioUE?si=BdI0b-NovWlBBn9B]
On Substack: What Business Leaders Can Learn From the ‘Mighty Midwest’
In this week’s Substack column, I laid out what today’s business leaders can learn from the Midwest. While the coastal cities chase flashy innovation, the Midwest runs on something more durable: fundamentals. Cities like Cincinnati are full of operators who value quality execution. One example I highlighted is Brian Niccol, Starbucks’ new CEO. He grew up in Philly, spent his years in Ohio and has become one of the most respected executives in the food industry. Now he’s leading Starbucks through a period of reset by dialing back—scaling smartly, improving quality, and resisting the pressure to chase growth for growth’s sake. I dig deeper into the lessons we can learn from this mindset driving the ‘operator economy.’
Read my full piece on Substack. [https://patrickmurphypa.substack.com/p/what-business-leaders-can-learn-from]
Building Resilient Communities
This week, I was honored to preside as officiant for Vows & Veterans, a free wedding and vow-renewal ceremony for veterans in Doylestown, Pennsylvania. The reception featured photography, live music, flowers, videography, cupcakes, and a catered lunch.
You can read about the event in the Bucks County Herald [https://www.buckscountyherald.com/news/veterans-responders-take-renew-wedding-vows-in-doylestown/article_b54718e0-ec01-44da-97cf-29aeb0189023.html] .
On Warrior Money: a Conversation with IAVA founder Paul Rieckhoff
During this week’s episode of Warrior Money on Yahoo Finance, we sat down with Army veteran and IAVA founder Paul Rieckhoff to discuss how military-tested skills, such as mission focus, teamwork, and resourcefulness, translate into boardrooms, startups, and public office.
Watch the full episode of Warrior Money here. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6zzJRLLVS10&list=PLx28zU8ctIRq4s21MFggvp9vDtChW2cM4&index=1]
Thank you all for your support. We couldn't do this without you. Check us out on Fox News 11am hour today.
Hon. Patrick J. Murphy
32nd Army Under Secretary

It's official...
I'm running to represent NY-12 in Congress! This is the district where I was born and raised, and the place that five generations of my family have called home.
Hi Peter, I'm Jack Schlossberg, and my grandfather, President Kennedy, is my hero.
In high school, I spent hours watching his speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. And that's exactly why I'm running for Congress.
This isn't going to be your average campaign — we’re at the forefront of a movement backed by real people who are ready for a new generation of leadership. I won't be bought or intimidated. Instead, I'll be relying on folks like you. So, if you're willing to be one of the first donors to my campaign, will you split a donation between myself and Real Texas PAC right now? I've always been passionate about politics — you can probably gather as much if you've seen any of my social media posts :) I pride myself on my hot (correct!) takes. But public service has always been my driving force. I come from a long legacy of public service, from my great-great-grandparents to my mother, Caroline Kennedy.
I have big shoes to fill. I've known it all my life. But this is even bigger than living up to my family name. This is about serving the people of New York — the city that shaped me into the person I am today.
Right now, our country is in crisis. Donald Trump and his buddies (my cousin RFK Jr. — to name just one) are tanking the economy, attacking free speech, and sowing distrust in decades of scientific research.
We need to revive empathy and effort. I want to be excited and feel hopeful about our future, and I want my fellow New Yorkers to feel the same way. I believe in a politics that works for the people it was intended to serve, and I'm ready to fight for it.
And Peter, I happen to think caring is cool.
None of this will be easy. But in the words of my grandfather, I'm doing this "Not because it is easy but because it is hard."
Together, we can build a new Congress and a New York City that works for everyone. Will you join our movement today by splitting a donation of any amount between my campaign and Real Texas PAC ? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?refcode=111325_1]
Talk soon,
Jack

You might be wondering: why should you care about a deep-blue seat in Chicago when MAGA is destroying the country and the GOP controls Congress?
Backed by thousands of grassroots donors from across the country, I was named a frontrunner by Chicago's Daily Herald in July -- and MAGA billionaires immediately took notice.

**RAISING ARIZONA (RED)** November has been an exciting month advancing freedom in Arizona, and we’re only getting started. In this off-year election, as is often true in the states, most Arizonans' ballots were full of bonds and overrides, and lacking major races that attract national interest. However, for those freedom fighters watching Arizona closely, there were significant wins that forecast even greater future successes. And the **Arizona Freedom Caucus** was an instrumental part of it. At the top of the list was successfully recalling the so-called “Republican” Mesa Councilmember Julie Spilsbury. Spilsbury’s offenses against the Arizona Republicans who put her in office had piled up, and she even became a public leader for “Republicans for [Kamala] Harris.” The successful recall is compounded by Spilsbury’s replacement, Dorean Taylor, a principled advocate for liberty, who was recruited by **Arizona Freedom Caucus** chairman Jake Hoffman. The recall victory is a preview of the exciting races and Freedom Caucus candidates on Arizona’s 2026 ballot. House Freedom Caucus member Congressman Andy Biggs is positioned to be the next Governor of Arizona. **Arizona Freedom Caucus** member Rep. Alexander Kolodin is challenging Democrat Adrian Fontes for Secretary of State. Sherriff Mark Lamb, who is running for Congressional District 5, received a strong endorsement from President Trump and the House Freedom Fund. With these critical endorsements, Sherriff Lamb is well on his way to the House of Representatives, where he will reinforce the excellent House Freedom Caucus members from Arizona, Congressman Paul Gosar and Congressman Eli Crane. While the prospects for advancing liberty in 2026 are thrilling, the greatest news is that our current ground-level battles are already expanding freedom today. Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap, an **Arizona Freedom Caucus** alumnus, is leading the critical work of bringing much-needed transparency and accountability in elections to the second largest county in the United States. Just off a highly successful 2025 election cycle, Recorder Heap is also tirelessly fighting to restore the full functions of his office so that he is able to secure Maricopa County’s elections. He is not only faithfully carrying out the duties of his office, but also shining a massive spotlight on the existing corruption. Amidst all these fights, the **Arizona Freedom Caucus** working alongside Turning Point USA (TPUSA) - which is headquartered in Arizona - is the offensive line necessary to secure generational wins for the cause of human liberty.Arizona is turning red in real-time!

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

Derek, last week was a big week for Democrats in every corner of the country. Just look at these states:
* In Virginia, Abigail Spanberger was elected the first woman governor of the Commonwealth with over 57 percent of the vote.
* In New Jersey, Mikie Sherrill won her race for governor with more than 56 percent of the vote.
* In New York City, Zohran Mamdani was elected mayor with over a million votes.
* In Pennsylvania, voters chose to retain three State Supreme Court Justices, with each receiving more than 61 percent of the vote.
* In California, voters approved Prop 50 with nearly 64 percent of the vote.

**No, none of these stats are a typo.** In states and cities nationwide, Democrats dominated in races up and down the ballot. Last week, voters sent a clear message to Trump and his allies: _We’re done with your attacks on our democracy and our economy, and we’re coming for Congress next._ At the DNC, we’ve spent 2025 organizing across the country, we’ve invested millions in state Democratic parties, and we’ve talked to voters in the bluest of blue and the reddest of red districts to make sure they are hearing Democrats’ message. **But here’s the truth: The work is just beginning. # [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=1957%2E791427%2EABBO69)
Friend, this is not an easy message to write.
As you know, I get a lot of hate from the far-right and conspiracy theorists of all kinds. I deal with constant harassment and threats of violence, both online and in real life.
And when folks like Donald Trump and Nancy Mace constantly attack me with baseless smears, **_the number of threats goes through the roof.**_
That’s why I do everything I can to ensure my safety and the safety of my campaign by hiring a security team.
But the thing is, security is expensive. Way more expensive than you may think. A lot of people assume that as a member of Congress, it is provided to me for free — it’s not.
So, I am coming to you today to humbly ask for your help in providing for the safety and peace of mind of my campaign.
If you can afford it, it would mean the world if you could chip in today and ensure that we have the budget to continue to afford our security detail.
We can’t take a laid-back approach when my safety and the safety of the people around me are on the line. We have to take every threat seriously.
**[Please, chip in $10 or whatever you can today to help us pay for security. I wish I didn’t have to ask. I wish we weren’t in this situation. But the far-right has made it so, and we have to protect ourselves.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-nov25.AgDe-P&refcode=em251114-1-180&t=2&akid=1957%2E791427%2EABBO69)
