High-profile restaurateur Stratis Morfogen **[pulled the plug on three new NYC establishments,](https://substack.com/redirect/5d5db61e-8a02-4ad1-9b39-d1c99b31893a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** including one in Midtown West, vowing "I'm not signing any more leases in New York" after Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani's victory, while fellow restaurateur Richie Romero halted new openings except for one East Village location where construction had already begun.
# Watch:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5d5db61e-8a02-4ad1-9b39-d1c99b31893a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/5d5db61e-8a02-4ad1-9b39-d1c99b31893a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Concerns over socialist policies and $30 minimum wage:** Both restaurateurs cite fears about Mamdani's "radical" proposals, particularly raising minimum wage to $30 by 2030, which Morfogen warns will "put fast-casual out of business" and cause a "$12 burger to go up to $22," as well as concerns about public safety given Mamdani's criticism of the NYPD and proposals to defund police, with Morfogen saying the policies "scare the s-t out of small business owners."

* **Soviet-era intelligence vessel still in service:** The Vishnya-class ships were built for the Soviet Navy in the 1980s for signals intelligence gathering via extensive sensor arrays with satellite transmission capability, and while seven remain in service with the Russian Navy primarily for intelligence collection, they are armed with AK-630 weapon systems and SA-N-8 surface-to-air missile launchers for self-defense, with customary international law permitting foreign military vessels to operate outside other nations' 12-nautical-mile territorial seas.

# **Legal group demands criminal probe into school district over alleged Democrat campaign rally**
A nonprofit legal organization is urging Virginia authorities to launch **[a criminal investigation into Portsmouth Public Schools](https://substack.com/redirect/df2c819b-de0f-47fd-abdd-8f7501d4ec85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after the district allegedly provided taxpayer-funded resources for a political rally featuring then-gubernatorial candidate Abigail Spanberger in August.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/df2c819b-de0f-47fd-abdd-8f7501d4ec85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Alleged legal violations:** The Liberty Justice Center claims the school system violated Virginia statute 18.2-112.1(B) governing misuse of public assets, which becomes a Class 4 felony when the value exceeds $1,000. The group also contends Spanberger's campaign failed to report the venue use as an in-kind contribution on required financial disclosure forms.
* **Event circumstances:** The August rally at I.C. Norcom High School occurred on the first mandatory work day for teachers preparing for the new academic year, with staff on the clock and school facilities utilized at no charge to the campaign. The Liberty Justice Center estimates services rendered--including facility rental, staffing costs, and maintenance labor--surpassed the $1,000 felony threshold.
* **District response:** Portsmouth Public Schools maintains administrators believed they were hosting an educational event rather than a campaign function, and that the principal instructed staff not to attend once the political nature became apparent. The district stated no public admission occurred and buildings were already operational, though email records show campaign officials distributed public RSVP links and requested additional classroom space.

The Liberty Justice Center has petitioned Attorney General Jason Miyares and Portsmouth Commonwealth's Attorney Stephanie Morales to pursue the matter, but neither office has indicated whether an investigation will proceed. Spanberger won the gubernatorial election last week.

body:
Tim has always been driven by values and service.
#
Peter,
This is Tim (in the winter hat with his mom and dad). Growing up in a small town of only 400 people, he learned early on in life the values of hard work, family, and caring for your neighbors through service.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=em_tw_20251114.Dl2zJF&refcode=em20251114-80&t=1&akid=80%2E34582%2EONWSRZ)
Long before he became Governor, Tim first served his country by enlisting in the Army National Guard while in high school, just two days after his 17th birthday. He went on to serve as a Guardsman for 24 years.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=em_tw_20251114.Dl2zJF&refcode=em20251114-80&t=2&akid=80%2E34582%2EONWSRZ)
Tim eventually turned to a new kind of service: teaching. His experience as a high school teacher is what ultimately inspired him to run for office (and it’s how he met his wife and fellow teacher, Gwen!).
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=em_tw_20251114.Dl2zJF&refcode=em20251114-80&t=3&akid=80%2E34582%2EONWSRZ)
Throughout his life, from soldier, to educator, to governor, Tim has been driven by putting our Minnesota values into action and helping make life better for others — that’s why he’s running for reelection.
**We have an opportunity to continue delivering progress for Minnesotans – but only if we hold onto this governor’s seat next November, Peter.**
**[Can Tim count on you to chip in $5 or more to help make it happen?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=em_tw_20251114.Dl2zJF&amount=5&refcode=em20251114-80&t=4&akid=80%2E34582%2EONWSRZ)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=em_tw_20251114.Dl2zJF&amount=5&refcode=20251114-80&t=23&akid=80%2E34582%2EONWSRZ)**
Thanks for all you do,
Team Walz

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dr. Kim Schrier for Congress
body:
As a pediatrician, Kim spent years caring for kids and families managing diabetes. [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119285621/582551539/693975070?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxY2U5ZDk1OS03YmMxLWYwMTEtODE5Ni02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Yejim-tFYZd5eO_E94uT7ga-O6bDHvcQDidSbymtVYQ=&emci=70751107-ecbf-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=1ce9d959-7bc1-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=15820338)
---
Peter,

Today is National Diabetes Awareness Day, and for Kim, _this fight is deeply personal._

As a pediatrician, Kim spent years caring for kids and families managing diabetes. And as someone who lives with Type 1 diabetes herself, she knows exactly what it means when politicians play reckless games with people's healthcare.

Kim has been a leading voice in Congress and fought tooth and nail against the GOP's relentless attacks on American healthcare. So far, she has:

✅ Fought to expand access to affordable insulin

✅ Introduced the bipartisan SCREEN for Type 1 Diabetes Act to raise awareness and expand early screening to help families detect and manage diabetes sooner

✅ Improved public education and prevention efforts

✅ Fought to ensure every American, _no matter their ZIP code or income, can access the care they need._

But once again, **Donald Trump is doing everything he can to undo the progress Kim has fought for.**

Earlier this year, his administration canceled **$400 million** in federal research grants, including crucial funding for the Diabetes Prevention Program— _one of the most successful public health studies in history that helped millions of Americans reduce their risk of Type 2 diabetes by over 50%._

But this isn't just about one program. It's part of a larger pattern; the same old attacks on science, healthcare, and the people who depend on them. But Kim knows Americans deserve better than Trump's dangerous games. clean_body: As a pediatrician, Kim spent years caring for kids and families managing diabetes. Peter, Today is National Diabetes Awareness Day, and for Kim, this fight is deeply personal. As a pediatrician, Kim spent years caring for kids and families managing diabetes. And as someone who lives with Type 1 diabetes herself, she knows exactly what it means when politicians play reckless games with people's healthcare. Kim has been a leading voice in Congress and fought tooth and nail against the GOP's relentless attacks on American healthcare. So far, she has: ✅ Fought to expand access to affordable insulin ✅ Introduced the bipartisan SCREEN for Type 1 Diabetes Act to raise awareness and expand early screening to help families detect and manage diabetes sooner ✅ Improved public education and prevention efforts ✅ Fought to ensure every American, no matter their ZIP code or income, can access the care they need. But once again, Donald Trump is doing everything he can to undo the progress Kim has fought for. Earlier this year, his administration canceled $400 million in federal research grants, including crucial funding for the Diabetes Prevention Program— one of the most successful public health studies in history that helped millions of Americans reduce their risk of Type 2 diabetes by over 50%. But this isn't just about one program. It's part of a larger pattern; the same old attacks on science, healthcare, and the people who depend on them. But Kim knows Americans deserve better than Trump's dangerous games. She'll always fight to protect access to care and to ensure that families have the tools and treatments they need to live full, healthy lives. But it's going to take all of us stepping up to hold this administration accountable. Thank you, Kim Schrier for Congress Rep. clean_body: Now let’s get back to work for the American people. | Finally, Fellow American. Democrats finally ended their political stunt, and the shutdown is over. As I've said since the Schumer Shutdown first began, shutdowns start with a bang and end with a whimper, and this one was no different. I'm glad that several brave Democrats joined Senate Republicans in voting to reopen the government. We can now stop this nonsense & get back to work for the American people. As we reopen the government, - not your hard-earned dollars (but if you have a couple of bucks to spare, we need all the help we can get to fight back against the millions Democrats are raising...) Fellow American, I won't sugarcoat this. Democrats won big in Virginia, California, and New York this year. The far-Left wing of the Democrat party is highly motivated, and we need to match their enthusiasm. Thanks, Fellow American. I am looking forward to reading your responses. Steve Daines P.S. The shutdown is finally over, and the first order of business is to hear from you, Fellow American. Steve Daines is a fifth-generation Montanan, life-long sportsman and father of four serving the people of Montana as their Senator. Steve is committed to always putting Montana first as he works to bring real change to Washington and fights for more jobs, less government and common sense solutions to get our country back on track. Senator Steve Daines | | Paid for by Steve Daines for Montana _

body:
After days of watching John sprint across this district, I wanted to reach out and share why this fight means so much to us.

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/eu6rOjxGdhmAea1WBurX5Q~~/AAUS1hA~/555HPQyZkkNdaYN-hA5s3LHf1c3xZ15hFoKtMuZzeU35YZGe0ejXAudvoXrKIF7FAzsPU9f6fqAp7bYfbPFZzzBJCsXPHKOARdmXPdUxgFjJvG3oc8TdZLatJ4h28lMi)
| | **Friend,** **After days of watching John sprint across this district, I wanted to reach out and share why this fight means so much to us.** Amber Padora here. I wanted to write to you directly because John has barely stopped moving this entire week. He’s been all over the district – from our wide-open plains to our growing towns to our suburban neighborhoods – meeting people where they are, listening to their struggles, and showing up with the same honesty and fire he’s had since the day I met him. It doesn’t surprise me that rural voters and working families connect with him so easily. John grew up farming with his grandfather, working long days, and living the same blue-collar life so many people feel forgotten in. He never had the privilege of being insulated from hard times – he lived them. And that’s exactly why he understands what’s happening in Colorado and across the country right now. **Families are getting squeezed from every direction.**
Housing costs have exploded.
Groceries are overwhelming.
Insurance premiums make no sense.
**And people are losing their jobs while everything keeps getting more expensive.** Through all of this, John is the **only** working-class candidate in this race. He works full time, raises our kids, runs this campaign with everything he has, and somehow still finds time to check in with me, help with homework, cook dinner, or just sit for a moment and be human. Sometimes I joke that he must have some kind of magic energy source hidden somewhere – but the truth is, **he just cares deeply**. And he doesn’t know how to quit when people are counting on him. John and I met in seventh grade. **I knew right away he was a little different**. There was something about him – this mix of empathy, stubbornness, and a kind of restlessness that came from wanting to make the world better, even before he had the words for it. Over the last 16 years, I’ve watched that spark turn into real work. I watched him push for criminal justice reform and treatment-based diversion programs.
I watched him advocate for medical marijuana access for children with epilepsy and for people like his father, who lived with chronic pain and multiple sclerosis.
I watched him show up at state capitols and in Washington to fight for policies that help working families breathe just a little easier.
I’ve seen him sacrifice, push, and keep going because he refuses to accept a world where people suffer needlessly. Today, he asked me to write this email because, truthfully, he simply doesn’t have a moment to spare. As I write this, we’re about to head out the door for another town hall in Larkspur. He’s been on the phone with supporters, donors, and organizations who believe in what he’s building. He’s earned the support of groups like Progressive Democrats of America – and he’s proud to be one of just seven non-incumbent U.S. House candidates chosen for the midterms. These are the same folks who have backed leaders like AOC, Greg Casar, Maxwell Frost, Zohran Mamdani, Summer Lee, and others who fight with their whole hearts. John and I often talk about how the word “progressive” has been turned into something negative by the political establishment and the people who want the Democratic Party to keep drifting right. But John has never been someone who runs away from his values. He runs straight toward them. He believes what President Theodore Roosevelt said – **“ A great democracy has got to be progressive, or it will soon cease to be either great or a democracy.” ** And right now, with **extremism rising** and our democracy **under threat** , we need progress more than ever. We need courage more than ever. We need candidates who don’t posture with guns in Christmas cards or turn politics into a spectacle – we need people who believe in peace, fairness, dignity, and opportunity for every child in this country. As Thanksgiving approaches, I’ve been thinking a lot about gratitude. I’m grateful for everyone who has stood with John from the very beginning – every volunteer, every donor, every person who’s opened their home or hosted an event or encouraged him to keep going. Your support is the reason he can travel this district, speak his truth, and build something real. clean_body: After days of watching John sprint across this district, I wanted to reach out and share why this fight means so much to us. | | | Friend, After days of watching John sprint across this district, I wanted to reach out and share why this fight means so much to us. Amber Padora here. I wanted to write to you directly because John has barely stopped moving this entire week. He’s been all over the district – from our wide-open plains to our growing towns to our suburban neighborhoods – meeting people where they are, listening to their struggles, and showing up with the same honesty and fire he’s had since the day I met him. It doesn’t surprise me that rural voters and working families connect with him so easily. John grew up farming with his grandfather, working long days, and living the same blue-collar life so many people feel forgotten in. He never had the privilege of being insulated from hard times – he lived them. And that’s exactly why he understands what’s happening in Colorado and across the country right now. Families are getting squeezed from every direction. Housing costs have exploded. Groceries are overwhelming. Insurance premiums make no sense. And people are losing their jobs while everything keeps getting more expensive. Through all of this, John is the only working-class candidate in this race. He works full time, raises our kids, runs this campaign with everything he has, and somehow still finds time to check in with me, help with homework, cook dinner, or just sit for a moment and be human. Sometimes I joke that he must have some kind of magic energy source hidden somewhere – but the truth is, he just cares deeply. And he doesn’t know how to quit when people are counting on him. John and I met in seventh grade. I knew right away he was a little different. There was something about him – this mix of empathy, stubbornness, and a kind of restlessness that came from wanting to make the world better, even before he had the words for it. Over the last 16 years, I’ve watched that spark turn into real work. I watched him push for criminal justice reform and treatment-based diversion programs. I watched him advocate for medical marijuana access for children with epilepsy and for people like his father, who lived with chronic pain and multiple sclerosis. I watched him show up at state capitols and in Washington to fight for policies that help working families breathe just a little easier. I’ve seen him sacrifice, push, and keep going because he refuses to accept a world where people suffer needlessly. Today, he asked me to write this email because, truthfully, he simply doesn’t have a moment to spare. As I write this, we’re about to head out the door for another town hall in Larkspur. He’s been on the phone with supporters, donors, and organizations who believe in what he’s building. He’s earned the support of groups like Progressive Democrats of America – and he’s proud to be one of just seven non-incumbent U.S. House candidates chosen for the midterms. These are the same folks who have backed leaders like AOC, Greg Casar, Maxwell Frost, Zohran Mamdani, Summer Lee, and others who fight with their whole hearts. John and I often talk about how the word “progressive” has been turned into something negative by the political establishment and the people who want the Democratic Party to keep drifting right. But John has never been someone who runs away from his values. He runs straight toward them. He believes what President Theodore Roosevelt said – “ A great democracy has got to be progressive, or it will soon cease to be either great or a democracy.” And right now, with extremism rising and our democracy under threat , we need progress more than ever. We need courage more than ever. We need candidates who don’t posture with guns in Christmas cards or turn politics into a spectacle – we need people who believe in peace, fairness, dignity, and opportunity for every child in this country. As Thanksgiving approaches, I’ve been thinking a lot about gratitude. I’m grateful for everyone who has stood with John from the very beginning – every volunteer, every donor, every person who’s opened their home or hosted an event or encouraged him to keep going. Your support is the reason he can travel this district, speak his truth, and build something real. And I’m grateful to know that when our kids and grandkids ask us where we stood during this moment in history, we’ll be able to look them in the eye and say we fought for universal healthcare, for affordable housing, for good schools, for safety, for fairness, and for a future that belongs to them – not to the wealthy few. John has the grit, the heart, and the determination to defeat Lauren Boebert and bring working people back into the center of our democracy. But we can’t do it alone. We’re up against enormous money pipelines from people who think they can buy this seat. They’re wrong – but only if we continue building a movement strong enough to match the moment we’re in. | | Fellow Conservative, Elon Musk is right. It isn't rocket-science. It's basic math. It's also a ticking time-bomb set by Joe Biden and Kamala Harris - in the form of 11.5 million illegals entering our country on their watch - one which will explode shortly after President Trump leaves office in 2029. While you and I have no doubt President Trump will deliver on his promise to secure the border, this threat will not go away. The truth is, without immediate action, these illegal aliens will be counted in the U.S. Census, which determines both the apportionment of seats in the House of Representatives _and_ the number of electoral votes given to each state. Whether they came because, four years ago, Kamala Harris and Joe Biden prompted them to "surge to the border" for asylum or because of blue-states offering sanctuary status, "free" health care, "free" cell phones, "free" housing, and "free" college...it doesn't matter. The result is the same. Your vote is _already_ being **watered down** in Congress. Your vote is _already_ being **watered down** in the Electoral College. And every day reports are popping up of non-citizens, illegal aliens, and convicted felons being registered to vote in cities and entire swing-states across the country, which means your vote may be fully **canceled out in future elections**. **_American elections should be decided by American citizens._** **[If you agree then please sign your"BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING" Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution so the chaos we're seeing now _never_ happens again in America.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkMGOozAMhp8m3EA4SQlz4NCWdjSHjlajFXuMTOK2kUiCSGBff0U1-wBzs3_Z1vf5z03f0E0uPD7RU2c2p5ek0dPiDAaayGQXQ0rPuE52JM1rfigBSpD7HBS2M7YRvKAOVCNAgpRQPDvT8DuQuhs60JtUo7qPIFrZKqnqVpAtXLdfAgAJStRCVDDaulUHoBGhhXFksl5ni5lSZWJItGyY3UYuhLhXMVQm-mLqnjnPiYkj41fGr-jR4Au5WmjbKhMZv87YyFY2iFzRWCsmrmv2OsV1McREf-rfy6_LwHizx56sWz0T_eX2nRj0M7pHYKLfmWsOb_rUv-vj7fhbnz7Pw6v7ugz617E8Dx_fa9kw0Z-Hj_K_aLF0dv7rpsmlRjFZPzy66WWRf_73reP_AgAA___OEYzK)** Because, here's the scary part: The last census took place in 2020. That was _before_ the 11.5 million illegal aliens who invaded our country under Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. To put it in context, there are only 8 states in America with a population over 11 million. So, it's as if the radical Left just imported the 9th largest state in America. That's more than North Carolina (10.8 million), Michigan (10 million), New Jersey (9.2 million), or Virginia (8.7 million). You get the picture. That's why urgent action is needed to pass a Constitutional Amendment to ban illegal aliens from voting and from being counted for purposes of congressional and electoral vote apportionment. The next census in less than 6 years away. If those 11.5 million illegal aliens are counted in the census or are allowed to vote in the intervening years, you and I simply won't have a country. **[It's vitally important that your representatives in Washington and in your state legislature hear this demand directly from you.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkMGOozAMhp8m3EA4SQlz4NCWdjSHjlajFXuMTOK2kUiCSGBff0U1-wBzs3_Z1vf5z03f0E0uPD7RU2c2p5ek0dPiDAaayGQXQ0rPuE52JM1rfigBSpD7HBS2M7YRvKAOVCNAgpRQPDvT8DuQuhs60JtUo7qPIFrZKqnqVpAtXLdfAgAJStRCVDDaulUHoBGhhXFksl5ni5lSZWJItGyY3UYuhLhXMVQm-mLqnjnPiYkj41fGr-jR4Au5WmjbKhMZv87YyFY2iFzRWCsmrmv2OsV1McREf-rfy6_LwHizx56sWz0T_eX2nRj0M7pHYKLfmWsOb_rUv-vj7fhbnz7Pw6v7ugz617E8Dx_fa9kw0Z-Hj_K_aLF0dv7rpsmlRjFZPzy66WWRf_73reP_AgAA___OEYzK)** Because, quite honestly, they think they can pull a fast one on you. They think you and I will be so relieved to see the border secure again and criminal illegal aliens deported, that you and I will be oblivious to this threat lying dormant under our very eyes. No way. My name is Rebecca Weber. I'm the chairwoman of AMAC Action. **AMAC Action is the most influential advocacy group in the country when it comes to standing for the values of conservative Seniors.** **We 've got 72 chapters and 300 volunteer delegates, who are the "feet on the street" advocates who contact Members of Congress and state legislators in their district offices.** **Moreover, our chapters and delegates help organize Town Hall meetings with elected officials and candidates to enable those locally of our 2,000,000 AMAC members to meet, hear, and question them.** **And you should also know that we now have more than 337,000 AMAC members who respond to our "calls-to-action" and weigh in with members of the ** **U.S. House and Senate, as well as their state legislators on the issues.** Quite simply, when we speak, Washington listens. **[And AMAC Action needs your help today in this do-or-die battle to pass a Constitutional Amendment to protect your vote from being canceled out by an illegal alien or a convicted felon.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkMGOozAMhp8m3EA4SQlz4NCWdjSHjlajFXuMTOK2kUiCSGBff0U1-wBzs3_Z1vf5z03f0E0uPD7RU2c2p5ek0dPiDAaayGQXQ0rPuE52JM1rfigBSpD7HBS2M7YRvKAOVCNAgpRQPDvT8DuQuhs60JtUo7qPIFrZKqnqVpAtXLdfAgAJStRCVDDaulUHoBGhhXFksl5ni5lSZWJItGyY3UYuhLhXMVQm-mLqnjnPiYkj41fGr-jR4Au5WmjbKhMZv87YyFY2iFzRWCsmrmv2OsV1McREf-rfy6_LwHizx56sWz0T_eX2nRj0M7pHYKLfmWsOb_rUv-vj7fhbnz7Pw6v7ugz617E8Dx_fa9kw0Z-Hj_K_aLF0dv7rpsmlRjFZPzy66WWRf_73reP_AgAA___OEYzK)** But I can't do it without you. **No matter what issue you care about the most, if you and I don 't have a secure, _honest_ elections... none of it matters.** Inflation. Illegal immigration. Violent Crime. Drug use. Homelessness. The 2nd Amendment. Out of control spending. Social Security and Medicare insolvency. Right to Life. Indoctrination in our schools. Now, here's the bad news: Most state constitutions grant voting rights to "every" citizen, open-ended language that liberal activists argue permits localities to authorize non-citizen and even illegal alien voting. States should amend their constitutions to instead permit "only" citizens to vote. But there's good news, too: Seven states have _expressly_ banned non-citizen voting already: Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Louisiana, North Dakota, and Ohio. **What 's more, voters approve of constitutional amendments to ban non-citizen voting by overwhelming margins. Nearly 77% of Ohio voters approved a measure in 2022, while nearly 63% of Colorado voters approved one in 2020.** This is a solution whose time has come. It's also about saving America. And it all starts with the straightforward premise that non-citizens and illegal aliens - no matter how many Kamala Harris and Joe Biden imported on their watch - should be banned from voting _and_ banned from being counted for apportioning congressional seats and electoral votes. | | | Hi Peter, **After a 134-day delay, Harrisburg finally passed a state budget.** ****The budget includes some important wins:
* More funding for education
* Wage increases for 8,000 homecare workers to at least $15/hour plus PTO
* Additional childcare funding
* And expanded support for Solar for Schools, a program led by WFP champion Rep Elizabeth Fiedler**.**

**But let’s be clear, Peter. This budget still falls short of what Pennsylvania’s working families deserve.** It misses a critical opportunity to invest in our state's future. There’s no new funding for home repairs or transit, no minimum wage increase, and no plan to raise new revenue — all while federal cuts loom that could push hundreds of thousands of people off Medicaid and double health insurance premiums. Pennsylvanians deserve better. And here’s the urgent part: **the budget for 2026–2027 is already being drafted.** If we don’t act now, it could fail Pennsylvania families the same way.
**[Write to your PA legislators today and tell them to support the “Tax Billionaires, Fund PA” plan — to close corporate loopholes, pass a digital ad tax, and tax billionaires’ unearned income so Pennsylvania can fund housing, schools, healthcare, and more.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39flXHMmeMQ4GTaibnjUGBRWeWnJXbIzDVva6xYM13L-TDvbjv-kzZtHgcO0OC-oMQNOnkPHsvWL_GJrhLbQ-04YGF45muXMBgXVLqpzmypa4cdUbeZGPeT0sFs8OuZBadmHxXchB9iBbGaQ-6lYX2a5hNHFqeE5h4XbtLN_rJ3JyNnlMFyYde_xgVyy8GjrXNkn1lOkJwGgGvoBGY6EUcloDcbVzV5gz55HU8cZmZMmNteLNSziG1SnbCUN4AG7DFrpo5A7fRPLmUzg6k9YPKcxXOaq1z_CYAmkMlpEsGspEnnruT4feS6_4fyigCIlbg/4ll/47mbGccqQMG5q7Ppy13GnA/h0/h001.26ihKlW5w3rbAclkI2rsVHKNf81odAQbIWz0Nsty95I)** **[Send a letter »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39flXHMmeMQ4GTaibnjUGBRWeWnJXbIzDVva6xYM13L-TDvbjv-kzZtHgcO0OC-oMQNOnkPHsvWL_GJrhLbQ-04YGF45muXMBgXVLqpzmypa-juYOahjlUbzYmdAge7l9zfCtu3rwHEbGGW88ypQxpO4IujeZaAoxUPV_MnwWbyB2c4KtQ89Ac7mhfVuiidLmCHEg0xHAadPvK28Cx7uSddZiGKUH-uZ3RxdysrOinshvRpkF1hosfkExS8wPiu0g3iScjEgesKTdjPS7Vzv7cRORwEF_vqBV4pVV4n_GRHhzliqmzWJl2-v0_R6tc0aqw/4ll/47mbGccqQMG5q7Ppy13GnA/h1/h001.tOo-vTRFWjLK8Dg2wF2j0LpdutoTDBYiSJ2UIAnE4rY)** It’s long past time for legislators in Harrisburg to stop playing the same political games and start pursuing common-sense ideas to increase revenue, like taxing passive income for the wealthy, taxing tech giants like Google and Facebook, and closing corporate tax loopholes. **The money is there. What’s missing is the political courage to put it to work for Pennsylvania's families, not let it line the pockets of the wealthy few.** That’s why, alongside our partners in the PAYBAC coalition, we launched the **Tax Billionaires, Fund PA plan** — a bold, fair revenue proposal to make the ultra-wealthy and big corporations finally pay their fair share. The plan would:
* **Close all corporate tax loopholes** : If a business operates in Pennsylvania, it should pay its fair share in taxes— no exceptions.
* **Pass a digital ad tax** : Big tech companies like Google, Amazon, Meta, and TikTok rake in huge profits from ads that clutter our screens. It’s time they pay sales taxes like smaller businesses do.
* **Tax Pennsylvania’s billionaires:** The wealthiest Pennsylvanians earn millions every day without lifting a finger. By taxing income from stocks, real estate, trusts, and royalties, we could generate billions for our communities.

Together, these reforms would generate at least $4 billion to invest in schools, transit, housing, and healthcare — the foundations that make Pennsylvania work for all of us, not just the wealthy few. **We know it’s still early in the process, but this is exactly when action matters. Lawmakers must put people before billionaires, and speaking up now can help shape the 2026–2027 budget before it’s finalized.** [**Write your legislators today and tell them to tax billionaires, and fund Pennsylvania’s future.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39flXHMmeMQ4GTaibnjUGBRWeWnJXbIzDVva6xYM13L-TDvbjv-kzZtHgcO0OC-oMQNOnkPHsvWL_GJrhLbQ-04YGF45muXMBgXVLqpzmypa-AsawSwoIjLgk6zQ_93zcsDzX0M_mhqAppFTeeeLnNlatu3fLUmQzFr1ATTq9b0rskzDmbxqFll_Nf4S4NATNDRDHBrz_6jWJFo8IsXO6kIdl_OHt9gz53ZPyGc9asySGQbsY4bqSM2HcvvPXH6Hs7lRa5LnQi2pcOkCxkxYWTX_WBs9aGN74mk3EldpFtBXuPd-sCcQgf0BvopsN3TvFM/4ll/47mbGccqQMG5q7Ppy13GnA/h2/h001.RIVY_L95LeqW0LQGj2XM-CGfbbv79iSeupBllL4ECnU) **[Send a letter »****](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39flXHMmeMQ4GTaibnjUGBRWeWnJXbIzDVva6xYM13L-TDvbjv-kzZtHgcO0OC-oMQNOnkPHsvWL_GJrhLbQ-04YGF45muXMBgXVLqpzmypa0QPMMsA_-JEBqI_wxyZhYIZ99GUUydM1qp1aTNlXWgD3DT_6_O7G2DOc_iOqOHIwi7MMB3cUG6ISOPo-aUv6ZovkBK7iR3DlxyuzEuFEnSd1enDwNHmOhqt9QEs8-Lcdhgr7ZtGZTX_xxzVfua0qHFDefkUxkICPuC0X8bkEQPE8eTyiRbqE42Eohk1dgJCmwccVbIKXIEx245SYKk938U/4ll/47mbGccqQMG5q7Ppy13GnA/h3/h001.bP4vc2f5DuTffBA0QeBbxaqg7Pe_RYT4v1J2FtA7R6w)** In solidarity, Rachie Weisberg

| | , November is National Family Caregivers Month, and I want to talk about the people we don't talk about enough – the family members caring for aging parents, disabled relatives, or sick loved ones while trying to hold down jobs and raise their own families. As a dad, I've watched friends and neighbors quietly struggle with this. They're exhausted. They're stressed about money. They feel guilty when they can't do it all. And they rarely get the support they need.More than 50 million Americans are family caregivers. Many are juggling full-time jobs while managing medications, coordinating doctor appointments, and providing round-the-clock care. It's physically exhausting and financially devastating.We need policies that actually help: **-** Paid family leave so people don't have to choose between caring for loved ones and keeping their jobs** -** Tax credits for caregiving expenses** \- **Better support services and respite care ** -** Expanded home healthcare coverage through Medicare and MedicaidIf you're a family caregiver, know this: you're not alone, and what you're doing matters. You deserve support, not just gratitude.Appreciate you, _Greg_ 💙🙏

# White House unveils South American trade deals
The White House **[unveiled trade pacts](https://substack.com/redirect/96db00d8-caee-433d-86e8-4096e8b703e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Wednesday with Ecuador, Guatemala, El Salvador and Argentina, slashing tariffs on U.S.-scarce staples like coffee, bananas and beef to ease consumer costs while shielding domestic industries from oversupply.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/96db00d8-caee-433d-86e8-4096e8b703e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Targeted Tariff Reductions** : Ecuador gains cuts on coffee, bananas and cocoa under a 15% baseline; Guatemala and El Salvador see similar breaks on qualifying produce amid 10% rates.
* **Argentina Beef Access** : There will be lower duties on beef imports without but no change in the quota of beef imports, alongside eased tariffs on meds, chemicals and tech.
* **Reciprocal Trade Commitments** : Trade partners pledged to improve trade interactions with the U.S. El Salvador will streamline its export regulations to the U.S by addressing non-tariff regulatory barriers, Argentina will give preferential access to U.S. goods and Guatemala has vowed not to tax U.S. digital products.
* **Environmental Safeguards** : Ecuador commits to robust protections against illegal logging, balancing import boosts with sustainability amid broader non-tariff barrier reforms.

* * *

# [Don't let the RMD trap limit your financial flexibility](https://substack.com/redirect/31fbb875-c40a-4d2f-a39c-80e721c0e245?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31fbb875-c40a-4d2f-a39c-80e721c0e245?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Most retirees take their Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) in cash -- and that often means more for Washington and less for you. Once you reach a certain age, the IRS requires that you begin taking distributions from your retirement accounts, whether you need the money or not. **[For many retirees, this can feel like a forced withdrawal that interrupts their long-term plans for preserving wealth.](https://substack.com/redirect/e99e23e1-84d9-4804-a52b-fbce9a52f5a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
However, few people realize there's another option available under IRS Code 408(m)(3). This provision allows certain types of precious metals, such as gold and silver, to be held within specific retirement accounts -- and in some cases, distributed in-kind rather than liquidated for cash. By understanding and utilizing this strategy, you can maintain greater control over your assets and potentially preserve more of your retirement's purchasing power.
**[The key is knowing how to structure your RMDs strategically](https://substack.com/redirect/31fbb875-c40a-4d2f-a39c-80e721c0e245?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** -- and how physical assets like precious metals can play a role.
Don't let the RMD trap limit your financial flexibility. Discover how to use IRS Code 408(m)(3) to your advantage and make your retirement assets work smarter for you.
**[Learn how to avoid the RMD trap-- and keep more of what's yours in this free guide.](https://substack.com/redirect/31fbb875-c40a-4d2f-a39c-80e721c0e245?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Claim your FREE guide here](https://substack.com/redirect/31fbb875-c40a-4d2f-a39c-80e721c0e245?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
# Trump played hardball and now Switzerland caves
In a surprise pivot from trade tensions, the **[U.S. and Switzerland struck a deal](https://substack.com/redirect/58c59d4d-662f-444e-b285-286c1341f8b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Friday to slash tariffs on Swiss imports from 39% to 15%, aiming to lure billions in manufacturing like pharmaceuticals and gold processing to American soil.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/58c59d4d-662f-444e-b285-286c1341f8b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tariffs Align with EU Rates** : The deal standardizes 15% duties on Swiss goods to match European Union levels, easing export burdens after July's punitive hike crippled Swiss growth forecasts.

[](https://substack.com/redirect/3a07ad16-ff98-4eee-bc50-4a78f5b93c9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Manufacturing Shifts to America** : Swiss firms commit to relocating production in surplus sectors--pharma, gold smelting, railway gear-- to the U.S. potentially sparking a U.S. job booms and erasing trade imbalances.
* **Roche 's Massive Investment Pledge**: Swiss pharma titan Roche vows a $50 billion infusion into U.S. facilities, accelerating the deal's push for onshoring amid broader export realignments.
* **Franc Surges on Optimism** : The Swiss currency jumped 0.4% against the dollar post-announcement, signaling market relief.

* * *
* * *
# Bitcoin's bloodbath continues as it drops to below $95,000
Bitcoin **[tumbled below $95,000 Friday,](https://substack.com/redirect/7adcf187-67c5-4464-8c51-778dfe3416ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** accelerating a four-day rout that has erased recent gains and rattled crypto markets, as overlapping investor fears from a sharp AI stock pullback spill over into digital assets.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7adcf187-67c5-4464-8c51-778dfe3416ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Four-Day Decline Accelerates** : After peaking at $107,000 early this week, Bitcoin's value plunged 3.5% in a single day to $94,896.03, signaling intensified selling pressure.
* **AI Stocks Trigger Spillover** : Resurgent worries over Big Tech's massive AI spending--hitting firms like Meta and Nvidia--hammered related equities, dragging down Bitcoin via shared investor bases.

[](https://substack.com/redirect/28eaff81-68c4-432f-b1e0-8e7b5984c522?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Crypto Firms Reel Hard** : Shares in key players tanked Thursday, with Strategy dropping 6%, Coinbase and Gemini each losing 5%, and Bitmine Immersion falling 5% amid the broader tech rout.
* **Record Outflows Surge** : Bitcoin ETFs recorded **[$870 million in net withdrawals](https://substack.com/redirect/ef0bcd9c-1e79-4d52-8a14-50277e430a91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Thursday, nearly $900 million total from crypto funds, signaling sharp investor retreat from the asset.
* **Liquidations Devastate Market** : Over $19 billion in crypto positions liquidated on Oct. 10 wiped $1 trillion from total market cap; another $1.3 billion vanished in the latest 24 hours alone.
* **🚨 UPDATE🚨: **At the time of publishing Bitcoin had regained some of its lost ground. **🔴 Bitcoin: $95,714 (⬇️ 2.19%)**

[](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac9acff-b572-493e-a23d-94705dc050d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
# StubHub tanks 24% after withholding 4th quarter guidance, spooking investors
StubHub's **[stock cratered 24% Friday](https://substack.com/redirect/e7f8f15b-d63f-4b07-8c32-e20ddf3096c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after the ticket resale giant withheld fourth-quarter financial guidance, overshadowing a strong third-quarter earnings beat and CEO Eric Baker's rosy outlook on live event demand.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e7f8f15b-d63f-4b07-8c32-e20ddf3096c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Earnings Exceed Analyst Projections**
Third-quarter revenue surged 8% to $468.1 million, topping estimates of $452 million, while gross merchandise sales rose 11% to $2.43 billion.
* **CEO Cites Demand Volatility**
Eric Baker highlighted "phenomenal" live event interest but blamed shifting schedules for unpredictable consumer trends.
* **Analysts Voice Surprise Concerns**
Wedbush called the no-guidance move unexpected, warning it fuels investor worries over short-term visibility despite maintaining an "outperform" rating.
* **2026 Outlook Looms Ahead**
StubHub plans to unveil next year's financial projections alongside fourth-quarter results, signaling their confidence in sustained growth.

[](https://substack.com/redirect/aca487ce-2e57-46d5-b4cd-4a4f2a62e7fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# **What is the lifespan of an AI Chip? It matters a lot more than you 'd think**
In the red-hot AI sector, where Nvidia's chips power a trillion data center frenzy, companies like Microsoft and Google are betting on six-year lifespans from their chips and GPUs to cushion costs--but "Big Short" investor Michael Burry has blasted those as projections as inflated, **[warning of rapid obsolescence](https://substack.com/redirect/ba3cfcf3-4b96-4ffe-81b3-d9fe0aed0d79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that could torch profits in as early as two years.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ba3cfcf3-4b96-4ffe-81b3-d9fe0aed0d79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Rapid AI Boom Accelerates** : Nvidia's data center revenue exploded from $15 billion pre-2022 to $115 billion by January 2025, fueling a three-year-old frenzy sparked by ChatGPT's late 2022 debut.
* **Tech Giants Extend Depreciation** : Oracle and Google peg AI servers lifespan at six years, while Microsoft ranges 2-6 years for equipment; Amazon trimmed some to five years amid faster tech evolution.
* **CoreWeave 's Resilient Rentals**: The GPU cloud provider reports full rebooking of 2020 A100 chips and 95% for 2022 H100s at near-original prices, defying obsolescence fears despite a 57% stock plunge from June highs.
* **Nvidia 's Annual Overhaul Pressures**: CEO Jensen Huang, referencing his own product line, quipped that older chips value will deteriorate as newer chips roll out, saying "When Blackwell starts shipping in volume, you couldn't give Hoppers away." Nvidia has shifted to yearly releases of new chips--echoing Burry's bearish short view on AI sustainability.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: How media monopolies could raise your streaming prices
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
How the potential Paramount-Skydance-Warner Brothers merger could raise your prices.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2699%2E4032634%2ELzcXdk)
---
Paramount, owner of CBS, Comedy Central, and a bunch of other channels, just merged with another giant company called Skydance. But apparently that wasn’t enough. The Paramount Skydance CEO now wants to buy up Warner Brothers. Reminder: Warner Brothers merged with Discovery — owner of Animal Planet, the Food Network, and HGTV — in 2022. So if this next mega-deal goes through, that’ll combine HBO, CNN, CBS News, Showtime, TBS, Comedy Central, TNT, Paramount+, TLC, HGTV, Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, Animal Planet, CBS Sports, Adult Swim, TeenNick, Boomerang, Cinemax, Cooking Channel, Food Network, Discovery Channel, Science Channel, The CW Network, Travel Channel, BET, MTV, VH1...**all into one giant company.** When all these media companies start combining, suddenly you have fewer options and less competition. **This is all a trap to hike your bills. We have antitrust laws to put a stop to this kind of corporate concentration — and I’m fighting to enforce them.** [**I’m sounding the alarm to protect consumers from these giant conglomerates that suppress competition and make prices skyrocket. If you’re with me in this fight, please chip in to support our campaign today so we can continue to stop monopolies from screwing over consumers.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3217?t=8&akid=2699%2E4032634%2ELzcXdk)

---

---

---
Let’s rewind to understand how this Paramount-Skydance deal even happened. If you remember, Paramount and Skydance had been wanting to merge for months, but needed approval from the Trump administration. That approval was conveniently approved after Donald Trump made a multimillion-dollar secret side deal with Skydance’s CEO, David Ellison. You might have heard of David Ellison and his father, Larry Ellison, before. Larry Ellison is a tech billionaire, and a close friend of Donald Trump’s. By taking over Paramount, David Ellison was able to take control of CBS and install what the execs are calling a “bias monitor” to watch what CBS journalists say. Now, Ellison is trying to buy Warner Brothers., CNN’s parent company. To top it all off, Trump is also tapping the Ellisons as part of the corporate group to run TikTok. So let’s get this straight: A couple billionaires who are buddy-buddy with Trump could control a huge percentage of our media and our social media platforms if these mergers and acquisitions continue without any accountability or enforcement of our federal laws. **That’s bad for American families, it’s bad for our free press, and it’s bad for our democracy.** [**I won’t stand for this — and I’m fighting back. If you’re sick and tired of media companies charging you more and more and more just to watch your favorite shows, and if you’re able to, please pitch in anything you can today to push back.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3217?t=14&akid=2699%2E4032634%2ELzcXdk) Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

body:

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/NPP_Ed_logo_RGB_green1-01.jpg]
Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.
Upcoming events
As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Pittsburgh%20School%20board%20forum%208.5x11.png]
Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students.
Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader.
With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color.
When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM
Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221
RSVP [https://click.everyaction.com/k/106793662/542679746/-435660973]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Allegheny%20judicial%20flyer.png]
Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot.
Your vote shapes our justice system!
Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager
Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms.

Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa]
Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th.
We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location.
#GoVotePA
SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [https://www.instagram.com/p/DJbyV6DPLdJ/]
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/7237344C447445787878394747342B75584E47375A57552F745265427662334B544A4A36505A58657A5871474B7A5A6E53705571424758325657365969365747/editor_images/WCM%20logo.JPG] #CourtsMatter
This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/DelCo_2.png] We are hiring!
Let's provide civic education together!
We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania.
Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote!
Positions start at $20 an hour.
Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org]
EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org]
News You Can Use
There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
* New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pittsburgh-mayor-election-2025-candidates-quiz]
* Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections/assistant/]
* Everything you need to know about mail voting [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-mail-ballot-how-to-request-fill-out-return] , becoming a poll worker [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide]
* Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pennsylvania-primary-election-day-2025-voter-information-registration]
* Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-commonwealth-superior-court-candidates] , vetting judicial candidates [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-candidate-vetting-guide]
* Guides to State College school board [https://www.spotlightpa.org/statecollege/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-state-college-school-board-anderson-huff-barlow-black-desmarais-mcternan-sogor] , Reading City Council president [https://www.spotlightpa.org/berks/2025/04/reading-city-council-president-primary-election-2025]
* Guides to voting as a college student [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-college-student-voting-guide]
En Español
* Guía para votar por correo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pensilvania-elecciones-primarias-2025-votar-correo-como-llenar] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/reading-concejo-municipal-primarias-elecciones-2025]
* Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-primarias-elecciones-2025-votar-informacion] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-elecciones-2025-como-convertirse-trabajador-electoral]
2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:
Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [https://penncapital-star.com/briefs/advocacy-groups-offer-training-for-pa-primary-poll-watchers/]
Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide/]
Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [https://fcfreepresspa.com/poll-workers-needed-for-pennsylvanias-2025-primary-election/]
6. Engage Your Elected Officials
Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise.
7. Vote in Every Election
Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility.
Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th!

clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed. The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error. Upcoming events As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls. [] Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students. Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader. With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color. When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] [] Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot. Your vote shapes our justice system! Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms. When: Monday, May 12, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] Social Media of the Week [] The deadline to request your mail-in ballot for the primary election is May 13th at 5PM. Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [] The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests. In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [] . [] We are hiring! Let's provide civic education together! We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania. Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote! Positions start at $20 an hour. Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org] EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org] News You Can Use There are things every one of us can do [] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last. 1. Educate Yourself Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally. Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more. Stay Engaged To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win. Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [] ) 3. Share What You Learn Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting. Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year! 4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work. Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above! 5. Become a Trained Poll Worker Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process. Here are some resources that may be helpful: Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [] Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [] Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [] 6. Engage Your Elected Officials Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise. 7. Vote in Every Election Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility. * **And our Florida Attorney General** — the guy who serves as our last line of defense against greed and corruption — is knee-deep in a massive corruption scandal for misusing _$10 million in Medicaid settlement funds meant to help Floridians._

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.
