| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

Atlantic Ave., Suite 200 Delray Beach, FL 33444 Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. ## **“The Mamdani of Florida”**
---
[|
---](https://kinterforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f6a723b5c3bc1add1f7a8ca4d&id=a5f7911d2d&e=d995135712)
| |

Today, someone referred to me as **"The Zohran Mamdani of Florida."**
They probably meant it as an insult, a way to label me as "too progressive" or "too disruptive" for Florida politics.
**Honestly? GREAT COMPLIMENT.**
---
| |

For those who don’t know, Zohran Mamdani is a NY State Assemblymember who has made a name for himself by doing exactly what politicians are _supposed_ to do, but rarely actually do:
* He fights unapologetically for the working class (like his historic win for taxi drivers).
* He refuses to take a dime of corporate or real estate money.
* He is unafraid to speak truth to power on foreign policy and demand an end to the genocide in Gaza.

---
| |

I am a Navy veteran running to flip FL-7, and if being "The Mamdani of Florida" means being a representative who is **unbought, anti-war, and dedicated to serving the people instead of the powerful** , then yes, that is exactly who I am.
Like Zohran, I am the only candidate in my race rejecting all corporate PAC and AIPAC money.
Like Zohran, I am building a movement grounded in solidarity and mutual aid, from food drives to direct advocacy.
And like Zohran, I am not afraid to stand alone if it means standing up for what is right.
**But to bring this kind of unapologetic leadership to Florida, I need your help. The establishment is terrified of this movement, and they are spending big to stop us.**

Thank you in advance for reading, and for **[anything you can give to help her Climate PAC continue electing courageous champions across the country.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119306374/582619908/2105508926?refcode=ea.c0910078-a8c1-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.c0910078-a8c1-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMwOTEwMDc4LWE4YzEtZjAxMS04MTk2LTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=07l-ez7d-qyxmZTPRFvzPWzfmOJDrVAzmrERED4fswk=)**

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119306375/582619909/2105508926?refcode=ea.c0910078-a8c1-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.c0910078-a8c1-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMwOTEwMDc4LWE4YzEtZjAxMS04MTk2LTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=07l-ez7d-qyxmZTPRFvzPWzfmOJDrVAzmrERED4fswk=)
Election Night proved something I've always known to be true.
**_If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together._**
My life has been shaped by standing with people who refuse to accept injustice. When we think back to the Civil Rights Act, the eight-hour workday, protections for women in the workplace — these victories didn’t feel inevitable. They felt impossible.
But I know from experience that the impossible becomes possible when people refuse to fight alone.
**In the late 60s and early 70s, I marched against police brutality targeting Black Americans.** I stood with Indigenous peoples demanding sovereignty. I watched communities risk everything to dismantle oppression. No single person could have achieved this. But together, we moved mountains.
**The anti-war movement in the 70s taught me that collective action can challenge even the most powerful forces.** I stood with millions of people to demand an end to an unjust war. Alone, none of us could have stopped it. Together, we did.
**The early 80s showed me that organizing can take many forms. My workout tapes weren’t just about burning sweat in leg warmers or leotards; they became a tool for change.** 17 million people bought those VHS tapes, and every dollar helped fund the Campaign for Economic Democracy — the organization my then-husband Tom Hayden and I created to protect our environment and strengthen our democracy.
**And now, in ACT III of my life, I’ve witnessed what’s possible when people unite to challenge an entire industry determined to put profit over our future.** Together, we've elected over 200 climate champions who refuse to be bought by Big Oil. These are leaders who will make a tangible difference in communities ravaged by cancers, poisoned water, and diseases we can barely pronounce.
In each of these movements, the lesson never changed. The impossible became possible because people came together. And on November 4, 2025, I saw that truth all over again.
Twenty-two victories in Virginia. History made in Georgia. Pennsylvania transformed. Climate champions elected from city councils to state legislatures and beyond in places desperate for change.
**I am so deeply grateful for what your support made possible. These results happened because thousands of people like you decided that going far together matters more than going fast alone.**
And we’re just getting started. We have a runoff in Texas and a special election for Congress in Tennessee. The 2026 midterms. A climate and democracy crisis that demands everything we have. And a big bully in the White House.
But I'm not worried. Because I've learned that when people truly come together, with courage and commitment and love for each other and this planet, we become unstoppable.
This is the work I will be doing for the rest of my life. And every morning, I wake up hopeful knowing I’m part of something bigger than one person.

clean_body: The impossible becomes possible when people refuse to fight alone. | | Below is a deeply personal note from actor and activist Jane Fonda. Thank you in advance for reading, and for = = Election Night proved something I've always known to be true. If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together. My life has been shaped by standing with people who refuse to accept injustice. When we think back to the Civil Rights Act, the eight-hour workday, protections for women in the workplace — these victories didn’t feel inevitable. They felt impossible. But I know from experience that the impossible becomes possible when people refuse to fight alone. In the late 60s and early 70s, I marched against police brutality targeting Black Americans. I stood with Indigenous peoples demanding sovereignty. I watched communities risk everything to dismantle oppression. No single person could have achieved this. But together, we moved mountains. The anti-war movement in the 70s taught me that collective action can challenge even the most powerful forces. I stood with millions of people to demand an end to an unjust war. Alone, none of us could have stopped it. Together, we did. The early 80s showed me that organizing can take many forms. My workout tapes weren’t just about burning sweat in leg warmers or leotards; they became a tool for change. 17 million people bought those VHS tapes, and every dollar helped fund the Campaign for Economic Democracy — the organization my then-husband Tom Hayden and I created to protect our environment and strengthen our democracy. And now, in ACT III of my life, I’ve witnessed what’s possible when people unite to challenge an entire industry determined to put profit over our future. Together, we've elected over 200 climate champions who refuse to be bought by Big Oil. These are leaders who will make a tangible difference in communities ravaged by cancers, poisoned water, and diseases we can barely pronounce. In each of these movements, the lesson never changed. The impossible became possible because people came together. And on November 4, 2025, I saw that truth all over again. Twenty-two victories in Virginia. History made in Georgia. Pennsylvania transformed. Climate champions elected from city councils to state legislatures and beyond in places desperate for change. I am so deeply grateful for what your support made possible. These results happened because thousands of people like you decided that going far together matters more than going fast alone. And we’re just getting started. We have a runoff in Texas and a special election for Congress in Tennessee. The 2026 midterms. A climate and democracy crisis that demands everything we have. And a big bully in the White House. But I'm not worried. Because I've learned that when people truly come together, with courage and commitment and love for each other and this planet, we become unstoppable. This is the work I will be doing for the rest of my life. And every morning, I wake up hopeful knowing I’m part of something bigger than one person. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you for being part of this movement. ✊ In solidarity, xx Jane | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. # State Senator Suzette Valladares Endorses Magsig for Senate
---
|
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** November 14th, 2025Contact: nathan@nathanmagsig.com
---
| | | | | | **(Clovis, CA)** \- Today, Nathan Magsig announced that State Senator Suzette Valladares endorsed his campaign for State Senate.
Senator Valladares issued the following statement, _“Nathan is a proven leader who spent his career strengthening communities, building affordable housing, and expanding opportunities for working families. Nathan will be a tremendous addition to the Senate Republican Caucus, bringing practical solutions, compassion, and proven experience to the State Senate. I’m proud to endorse him.”_

Magsig released the following statement:
_“I’m honored to have Senator Valladares’ support. Her leadership and her commitment to strengthening California’s families reflect the very best of public service. As I continue this campaign, I remain focused on delivering real results for our Valley by protecting our water, supporting our farmers, and ensuring safer, stronger communities for the next generation.”_
The endorsement follows the recent news that State Senator Shannon Grove, the current representative for State Senate District 12, backed Magsig’s campaign for State Senate. Senator Valladares now joins dozens of Senate, Assembly, and Central Valley leaders in endorsing Magsig’s campaign.
View the full list of endorsements [HERE](https://nathanmagsig.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=566959e132b9980afc6311201&id=92991617db&e=6cdbd718cb)
---
| | ###
Nathan Magsig is a current Fresno County Supervisor, former Mayor of Clovis, and is running for the 12th Senate District. His family, wife Julie and their three children, reside in Clovis, CA.

That’s why I’m running for the U.S. Senate - because Americans need a battle-tested former Navy SEAL, like me, ready to take the tough 3:00 a.m. calls that are commonplace at the highest levels of government. My opponent? She’s never taken a 3 A.M. call that didn’t come with a donor list attached. I’m Adam Schwarze—former Navy SEAL Officer, Marine Corps veteran, lifelong Minnesotan. I’ve done nine combat deployments across 70 countries. I’ve led men when the margin between life and death was measured in seconds. Minnesota doesn’t need another career politician who reads a poll at 3:00 A.M. America needs another Senator who has **already answered the 3 A.M. call —and brought everyone home. The left’s most recent internal poll shows a generic Republican within 2 points. That means this seat is flippable—but only with the help of grassroots conservatives like yourself. You must step up now if we’re to have any chance of flipping this seat for the first time since 2008. Could you I have a story to tell and a lot of fight in me, but the one thing we don’t have is money. I’m not backed by Hollywood or D.C. consultants. I’m backed by conservatives like you.**** Every dollar received by my campaign sends a message to the national GOP:Minnesota is in play. Because when the next 3 A.M. crisis hits—whether it’s a border surge, a riot, or a cyberattack— The American people deserve a U.S. Senator who’s already been there. body:

Peter,

We’re witnessing it every day: despite the so-called ceasefire agreement,
Israel continues to drop bombs, block aid, and kill Palestinians in Gaza.

In the words of Justice Democrats’ Rep. Rashida Tlaib, “The Israeli
government’s genocide in Gaza has not ended, and it will not end until we
act.”

That’s why she just introduced a resolution in Congress to formally
recognize this genocide and push the United States to meet its legal
obligations to prevent and punish it.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140967?t=1002&akid=37194%2E1203867%2EaRPLwf ]Will you urge your member of Congress to sign onto Rashida’s resolution
NOW?

By giving Israel $30 billion in weapons over the past two years, the
United States has failed miserably in our obligation to prevent genocide.
As Rashida said, “Impunity only enables more atrocity.”

It’s time for our government to stop sending weapons to Israel and start
prosecuting the officials responsible for these war crimes, so that this
genocide truly ends once and for all.

H.Res.876 would do just that, and right now, it’s backed by 20 cosponsors,
including every single Justice Democrats-endorsed incumbent: Summer Lee,
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar, Ayanna Pressley, Delia C. Ramirez,

# **Iowa school aide sues after being fired for Charlie Kirk Facebook comment**
A former Knoxville Community School District employee has filed a federal lawsuit claiming her termination **[violated constitutional rights](https://substack.com/redirect/c06a4c66-e25b-4e33-bb75-01fdeb6a3e9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after she posted a personal Facebook comment about slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Stacey Sumpter, a special education associate, was dismissed two days after writing "goodbye" on her private social media account in response to the Sept. 10 assassination.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c06a4c66-e25b-4e33-bb75-01fdeb6a3e9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Swift Termination:** District officials called Sumpter into the principal's office on Sept. 11 after receiving community complaints, then suspended her that evening and terminated her employment the following morning. Superintendent Cassi Pearson cited the post's language as "not respectful" and displays "hatred" in the termination letter.
* **Constitutional Claims:** Sumpter's legal team argues the district violated her First Amendment rights by punishing protected political speech made as a private citizen off-duty. The lawsuit contends her comment neither threatened anyone nor incited violence, and did not identify her workplace or occur during school hours.
* **Growing Legal Pattern:** Sumpter joins at least two other Iowa educators who have sued their districts over Kirk-related social media posts, with numerous others across the country facing similar situations for their conduct.

* * *
# **JFK 's grandson faces scrutiny over deleted Nazi salute video amid congressional run**
Jack Schlossberg, President John F. Kennedy's only grandson, is under fire after the Washington Free Beacon uncovered a deleted January Instagram video showing him **[performing a Nazi salute](https://substack.com/redirect/4478d992-2c77-478a-9730-df0c77dee4ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** multiple times. The 32-year-old announced his candidacy for New York's 12th Congressional District seat this week, seeking to replace retiring Democratic Rep. Jerry Nadler.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a7b1f7c4-2d92-4c4a-9fb2-79cd637633a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Musk Mockery Gone Wrong:** The video apparently aimed to ridicule Elon Musk, who faced accusations of performing a Nazi salute during President Trump's January inauguration, though Musk has vigorously denied the claim. Schlossberg repeatedly performed the gesture while saying "Yo, check this out" to the camera.
* **Additional Controversy:** The Beacon also reported Schlossberg posted a since-deleted recipe for a "MAHA energy ball" containing "Jew blood (ashkenazi not Sephardic)" and semen, apparently targeting his relative, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Schlossberg's father is Jewish, making the posts particularly inflammatory.
* **Social Media History:** The congressional candidate has gained notoriety for provocative online content including satirical political videos and shirtless posts. His campaign declined to comment on the resurfaced footage.

* * *
# **Manhattan therapist claims Trump Derangement Syndrome affects three-quarters of patients**
Manhattan psychotherapist Jonathan Alpert told Fox News that "Trump Derangement Syndrome" represents a genuine clinical issue affecting most of his practice, describing it as "the defining pathology of our time." The mental health professional said approximately **[75% of his patients display symptoms](https://substack.com/redirect/66e51d7e-c5ca-418c-9c6a-e923da43f068?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of obsessive fixation on President Donald Trump within minutes of their sessions.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/08c9a019-de64-44f5-8529-d00d02972819?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Clinical Symptoms Observed:** Alpert reports patients exhibit anxiety-like behaviors including persistent intrusive thoughts, sleeplessness, compulsive news monitoring and emotional dysregulation triggered by Trump's image or mentions. One patient told him she couldn't enjoy vacation because seeing Trump on her device left her feeling emotionally triggered.
* **From Politics to Pathology:** The therapist initially dismissed TDS as simple ideological disagreement but now recognizes clinical patterns resembling obsessive-compulsive spectrum disorders. In a Wall Street Journal op-ed, he described the condition as "obsessive political preoccupation" where a political figure becomes the focal point for heightened distress and compulsive behavior.
* **Widespread Impact:** Alpert said the Trump-focused symptoms emerge rapidly in sessions, with most affected patients bringing up their feelings about the president within five minutes.

The term "Trump Derangement Syndrome" was originally coined by Trump supporters to criticize what they view as irrational opposition to the president.

# **Left-Wing activists launch campaign against Senate Democrats over shutdown**
**[Indivisible](https://substack.com/redirect/a8e8b93e-4fb5-48e2-85d4-36fdcca65231?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , a progressive organization that organized the massive "No Kings" protests against President Trump, announced its **[biggest challenge effort](https://substack.com/redirect/364089f4-e18a-47c9-b9b7-8a841536a9be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** targeting Senate Democrats who voted with Republicans to end the historic government shutdown. The George Soros-funded group is demanding Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer step aside and vowing to support challengers against what co-founder Ezra Levin called "weak and cowardly" incumbent Democrats.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/408b7a38-ac2f-4482-b97f-94c8a04e80c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Declaring War on Moderates:** Indivisible criticized Democrats for "surrendering" after nearly six weeks of shutdown, arguing they abandoned momentum from strong election results and record-breaking protests.
* **Schumer Under Fire:** Multiple progressive voices including California Gov. Gavin Newsom called the deal "pathetic" and a "surrender," while DNC Chair Ken Martin praised the minority of Senate Democrats who opposed the vote. "Indivisible is ready to clean house and build a party that actually has the energy to act like an opposition," Lean Greenberg, co-founder and co-executive director of Indivisible said.
* **Primary Threat Details:** The campaign seeks candidates with "clear commitment to abandon the status quo of feckless leadership" and use all available tools to fight Trump's agenda. Indivisible, which launched in 2017 and has **[received over $7.5 million](https://substack.com/redirect/107ff6b8-442c-4309-bdd5-ebda5ec5ef26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** since from large foundations, describes the effort as its most ambitious primary program to date with endorsements expected in coming weeks.

---
Fellow Conservative,

Imagine, for a moment, **switching shoes with an active-duty Navy SEAL.**

The satellite phone rang at 3:00 a.m. local time.

You’re in a 20-foot shipping container turned command post, somewhere in the Horn of Africa you never see on a map.

_**No staff. No teleprompter. No second chances.**_

One of our teams was pinned down.

Bad guys closing in.

Decision time: **extract now and risk the helo, or hold and risk the men.**

You make the call. You get every American home.

_**That’s what a real 3 A.M. decision feels like.**_

_[](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=c8c650e22f874eb6b45d58b96e52ff5f&_e=6CyeGcXfVhdGpZnHOyLsNfIe5LnsgNNLi691wQSa1kiU-0hFwYQ21mtnx3iykcxiqtICQJ_LDnDzmp8h6p10PVt3Zrvvy84WP7SM2n2T3LLppoRjIGMaN64rE9bRop11dswA37ym702E_CHDYDVp5e3dg_SlqkPJUS0buUbelWA6gUpRXy9hf_UjJs7QdivJrn3uh1_4bzv5PH9gQ1jAzCDkmznsJP8DW_yknTkxg8e_1uexiYtuwHNoMoa2erGtan5XsJb3jJH2zhtR7D81yG08gq0P-57ijCNxVGU1iNkzBN5eDzs7yYVvvUnc64zxUoMXl8Xw3FvE2DipSym1zKYUhewT4wzgOxM6kOoSQYXTcsQci04lR9FBxV0WsB7bC145IaZOqputeLKwzxiQyZpbco6gYb6UeN2n90N9_sKvdPl3gH1yjhQvsuQlXAkeG2qIdPOS6_4ek6CGv3P6d0kjXmX8sK0gkVzlhH_9JUIlkj-BnZCv671YmuyxgjLvt47OjQy5iM04UMsERLnhiqm_ZD2fjpckc822xSFJAU1ZuSKUPJHXdJ2-m-aMnGBGKe99SFBvWrp9EvcAEF18MfNE8AbNKRwQxlMvKFCm1Lc0KzIdHzgOyjuepP5fw8Bv2MD3fxagfmcHWCnipluyme7e_unENWA2ZBfuf9F_x1qo9e7SZcnvq56CTz_SC6FZIPme7L42rMZLcUViERQN16s7wK8nMxSzshlJHxmUYAE%3D)_
Now, Minnesota faces its own 3 A.M. moments—only the phone is ringing in **Minneapolis, St. Cloud, Duluth.**

1. **_A 74% spike in carjackings since 2020._**

2. **_Illegals with criminal records released into our neighborhoods because Walz-Flanagan sued to defund ICE detention._**

3. **_Small-town hospitals are closing because state mandates crushed rural budgets._**

But this isn’t just happening in Minnesota - it’s happening all across the country. In big cities, small towns, and in state capitals, with out-of-touch career politicians leading the charge.

name: David Hogg
subject: A 401(k) for democracy
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
The work we do today decides who controls power for years to come.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20251114-1-b&t=1&akid=2836%2E587540%2ErgbUw3)
Hi Peter. David here. This is going to be a longer email, so let me get right to it:
I’ve been thinking a lot lately about what it takes to build long-term political power — the kind that lasts beyond one election cycle. And honestly? It works a lot like a long-term investment. _(Don’t worry — I promise I won’t finance-bro out on you.)_
Think of your support for Leaders We Deserve like a 401(k). You contribute steadily over time, and those investments compound into long-term security. The difference is that instead of building a retirement account, you’re building a safety net for American democracy — by helping transform the Democratic Party from the inside out.
Every dollar you invest today helps replace complacent career politicians with a new generation of young leaders who bring urgency, discipline, and decades of fight ahead of them. That’s exactly why we invest so heavily in states like Texas, Florida, Georgia, and Arizona. A dollar spent helping a young candidate in those states in 2026 can have the impact of spending ten times as much in 2030 — when those same states will have gained 4–5 congressional seats and 4–5 electoral votes each, and when we _must_ win legislative control to avoid being gerrymandered into permanent minority rule.
Yes, we’ll work to flip legislatures and congressional seats in 2026. But we also have to plant seeds where future majorities will be decided. Most political organizations operate on four-year timelines, which forces them to focus only on what can be won right now. We can’t afford that. We have to build our future bench in emerging purple states today so we’re not just reacting to power being taken from us, we’re preparing candidates to win the new seats Texas, Florida, and other Sun Belt states are on track to gain.
For too long, Democrats have tried to “time the market” of political change investing emotionally. Meanwhile, Republicans have spent 40 years investing steadily, the political equivalent of consistently investing in the S&P; 500\. They never stop, no matter whether the environment is favorable or not, no matter who the president is or who has majorities in Congress. Over time, those investments compound. That's the beauty of young candidates. They have the most valuable thing one can have when it comes to investing or making change: time.
It’s time for Democrats to build long-term, compounding political power too. That’s the work Leaders We Deserve is doing, and your investment is what makes it possible.
And just like any investment, $5 today matters more than $5 tomorrow. The earlier you invest, the greater the return, and last week’s election proved just how far early support can take young leaders. With momentum building, our mid-month deadline tomorrow at midnight, and the midterms less than a year out, now is when investing early matters most.
Because building a new generation of leaders works like a 401(k) — steady, small contributions adding up over time — the best way for you to make a real impact is by committing to a monthly recurring contribution.
**[If you’re able today, will you start a monthly recurring contribution of $5 or whatever feels right to invest in our 401(k) for Democracy?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251114_1_mm_401k.nFoxSU&refcode=em20251114-2836-b&amount=5&t=29&akid=2836%2E587540%2ErgbUw3)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251114_1_mm_401k.nFoxSU&amount=5&refcode=em20251114-2836-b&t=30&akid=2836%2E587540%2ErgbUw3)**
_Use the links in this email to start a recurring contribution to Leaders We Deserve._
Leaders We Deserve is just over two years old — and because of grassroots donors like you, we’ve already:
* Elected a young, bold, progressive mayor in New York City
* Supported Representative Dante Pittman in his run that broke the Republican super majority in North Carolina
* By just 74 votes, defeated a candidate in Texas who had previously voted to arm teachers and secured victory for Texas Senator Molly Cook
* Replaced ineffective Democrats with young progressive fighters
* Ran year-round organizing efforts to sustain our work
* Built one of the strongest benches of young leaders in the country and an intergenerational movement standing with them
* Forced the Democratic establishment to make room for the next generation and take our power seriously

body:
| | | Friend, When I was serving in Iraq, there were moments when my life flashed before my eyes. I was in the sky in a helicopter being shot at, and we could go down at any time. **In those moments, I leaned on my faith in Christ more than ever.** My Christian faith got me through the toughest moments serving in Iraq. _Even when my life was on the line, my faith kept me strong._ Trusting in something bigger than me has been pivotal in my life, and that’s why I’m so passionate about this fight. **Right now, the woke Left is trampling on our Christian values by forcing us to accept things that we know go against our beliefs.** I won't stand by it. I’m calling on you to join me in defending religious freedom for EVERYONE to be able to live according to their faith without politicians intervening.

If you've been waiting for the moment when the ground finally shifts beneath the Trump White House -- when long-buried secrets, sealed records, and political pressure collide with raw math -- then start this video from the very first second.
Because David Shuster walks you through a milestone Washington has been dreading for years: **the 218th signature on the discharge petition to force the Epstein files to the floor.** Not a Democratic majority. Not a procedural gimmick. A bipartisan revolt.
It begins with the swearing-in of **Adelita Grijalva** , completing the Democratic roster and making the target number reachable. But the real shockwave is what happens next: **four Republicans cross the line** , joining every Democrat to put their names on a petition the Trump White House has been desperate to kill.
Two hundred eighteen signatures.
The exact number required to force a vote.
The exact number Trump never thought anyone could assemble.
And the timing couldn't be more dangerous for him.

Shuster breaks down what that means, who wrote it, and why one email referencing a girl who "spent hours at my house with him" is sending shockwaves through Congress.

---|---|---
Then the bombshell: an Epstein insider confirms **every room -- in every mansion -- was wired for recording.** The New York townhouse. The Palm Beach estate. All of it. For years. Without anyone knowing.
That's why the panic is exploding inside the Trump White House.
Shuster takes you inside the extraordinary meeting where Trump's Attorney General, Deputy AG, and FBI Director haul Rep. Lauren Boebert into the _White House Situation Room_ -- the same secure bunker used for the Bin Laden raid -- to pressure her not to sign the petition.
She didn't cave. Others didn't either. And now the vote is unavoidable.
This episode is fast, sharp, fearless, and packed with revelations. It captures the moment Washington tipped: when four GOP defectors, one new member, and one historic petition cracked open the door to full Epstein transparency.
If you want the truth, you watch this. Now.

subject: They came for my neighbors
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Brent Hennrich for Washington
body:
| | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMU_BeZcmRBr16dPjlrMKhhjiC51ataw3Peft1wIO87ITSxjytRqnk5Se65PvvR0SC1Vi60eIcmGaf4kR6MPJnbRGd2XwIrhDn8ZZ-Z4PPuO0Vx2PdmM8zh_l0Ht__s0eBGtkgaBvDRFpB7S-GYfgUlKcY1NitjYcaHwB1DxoLAq9hJgOU0J9oJpFZrNMuI3kxOOZXihQRKOzrBksGrG_JEI/4ll/F-EoNsN0QPGafaMUiXdPPw/h0/h001.SDX29vlTGVJsE4gKQEz05uyJJjT1rFeDSdasztllvoY)
---
Peter,

Monday afternoon, 4:10pm. My daughter slammed through the front door screaming: _"Dad, ICE is on our block!"_ For a split second I was confused. Ice? It's November, not even that cold yet. Then my wife Amber yelled up from outside: _"Brent, are you coming? ICE is down by the mailbox."_ And it hit me like a punch to the gut. I grabbed my jacket, grabbed two phones, and ran outside in camera mode. Amber was already checking that the neighborhood kids had their US Passport Cards on them, trying to get them inside to safety. The kids wanted to watch what was happening down the block. I went into full dad voice: _Get inside. Lock the door. Don't open it unless your parents call and tell you it's safe._ Then I walked down toward the mailboxes where a dark grey F-150 was parked. Someone told me they'd seen a man with his face covered wearing a tan bullet vest with yellow lettering getting into the truck. I took photos. The windows were tinted too dark to see inside. At 4:14pm, the truck drove away.
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqv6r8GR7zKbLdKY8JcRsBH8aQhQzL-6XFLiJ1IzrYZqHcVu3_2xEWSSvdjjDmkiSUBu4iWO7luBexmcUL1xzaACEZfP_AMHbOi0MykFOpAeIEUgzWy7RYipGLZ1Q8gFYkyDR2-jSGucUZM64RFhX9ifFyxzrLmJdmTqUCOjybCuyMZnmegDNr8Id01Tq1QTEGfsMkWyDWou9peWZ0srVnaC8nqsThcmEKtGOjrthAkFMxN_vfS5mn0K8h5MztHJqBllxu-l-0zSX-oh2OQRtmapVub2MMwSRE4DwkASQMa2fmC3OwokolNXv2fdgholpFbaIIsSHwCw-JEJJ5uVDVgs/4ll/F-EoNsN0QPGafaMUiXdPPw/h1/h001.VjLqcTplQW9qm5QsYWbLDHi-SnxSJKMerKoQ2BpdpCU)
---
This was the first time I've ever seen ICE doing enforcement operations in our neighborhood... **In our neighborhood where kids play outside and families gather and people are just trying to live their lives**. And here's what you need to understand: **Marie Gluesenkamp Perez voted for the Laken Riley Act** - the legislation that gave Trump the foundation he needed to build his criminal paramilitary force. She **signed a resolution thanking ICE** for doing a "good job" even as reports poured in of extrajudicial, warrantless kidnappings happening across the country. She has **voted multiple times to increase ICE's budget**. They now have more funding than most standing armies. Marie voted to create this nightmare. And she still defends it.
---
[ **HELP PROTECT OUR NEIGHBORS** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqv6r8GR7zKbLdKY8JcRsBH8aQhQzL-6XFLiJ1IzrYZqHcVu3_2xEWSSvdjjDmkiSUBu4iWO7luBexmcUL1xzaACEZfP_AMHbOi0MykFOpAeILOZfMLHCYQuGPrGoZWn7r2X83VLH9QzG0yYAjVJRg0wK0FodmYtsg1aV1zJkDIbhBVd64hzpqWSFbP2ZXOLEI_TyiWycml_jM6YXXq0X-wnlKLlY6dE0AU6lIFE-Cr0wPgKXUz0tNPvReKaaGPAGq2cbvxhNlVmGl_zDc_VqzyRn1KJoqvPbDcBFxXVrPIBkpd7qzhmYR1ZV7CLYXpz5AO4n0ViBH30NAzBQ6iDrkyT/4ll/F-EoNsN0QPGafaMUiXdPPw/h2/h001.vGvsb1mYvqo81NSoxwm1O-ZGk8LPh4nVa9VmNoC6hvE)
---
As I stood on my street taking photos of that truck, all I could think about was my neighbors. About the families on this block who now have to wonder if they're safe in their own neighborhood. But my daughter could follow me down the block to record what was happening without fear because the color of her skin isn't what ICE is looking for. These families that are basically family to mine after living so close for so long. All the kids have grown up together and are in and out of my house all day on weekends and after school. About the kids who saw armed agents in tactical gear and will remember that fear. **This isn't some abstract policy debate happening in Washington D.C. This is happening on my block**. To people I know. To families who are part of our community. **I'm running for Congress because I will always defend our neighbors against this rogue agency.** No excuses. No political calculations. clean_body: | | Peter, Monday afternoon, 4:10pm. My daughter slammed through the front door screaming: "Dad, ICE is on our block!" For a split second I was confused. Ice? It's November, not even that cold yet. Then my wife Amber yelled up from outside: "Brent, are you coming? ICE is down by the mailbox." And it hit me like a punch to the gut. I grabbed my jacket, grabbed two phones, and ran outside in camera mode. Amber was already checking that the neighborhood kids had their US Passport Cards on them, trying to get them inside to safety. The kids wanted to watch what was happening down the block. I went into full dad voice: Get inside. Lock the door. Don't open it unless your parents call and tell you it's safe. Then I walked down toward the mailboxes where a dark grey F-150 was parked. Someone told me they'd seen a man with his face covered wearing a tan bullet vest with yellow lettering getting into the truck. I took photos. The windows were tinted too dark to see inside. At 4:14pm, the truck drove away. | This was the first time I've ever seen ICE doing enforcement operations in our neighborhood... In our neighborhood where kids play outside and families gather and people are just trying to live their lives. And here's what you need to understand: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez voted for the Laken Riley Act - the legislation that gave Trump the foundation he needed to build his criminal paramilitary force. She signed a resolution thanking ICE for doing a "good job" even as reports poured in of extrajudicial, warrantless kidnappings happening across the country. She has voted multiple times to increase ICE's budget. They now have more funding than most standing armies. Marie voted to create this nightmare. And she still defends it. As I stood on my street taking photos of that truck, all I could think about was my neighbors. About the families on this block who now have to wonder if they're safe in their own neighborhood. But my daughter could follow me down the block to record what was happening without fear because the color of her skin isn't what ICE is looking for. These families that are basically family to mine after living so close for so long. All the kids have grown up together and are in and out of my house all day on weekends and after school. About the kids who saw armed agents in tactical gear and will remember that fear. This isn't some abstract policy debate happening in Washington D.C. This is happening on my block. To people I know. To families who are part of our community. I'm running for Congress because I will always defend our neighbors against this rogue agency. No excuses. No political calculations. #
# **Working Pennsylvanians Are Getting a New Tax Credit**
**** This week, Senator Hughes was in Harrisburg to get the state budget passed. The Senate Republican budget impasse ended on Wednesday when state Senators and Representatives passed a bipartisan budget that delivered for affordability, education, community safety, jobs, and no tax increases. The new state budget includes a new [Working Pennsylvanians tax credit](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100170996.172546.27&gen=1&mailing_linkid=16081) for working Pennsylvanians making less than $60,000 a year. Pennsylvanians will be able to file for the tax credit when they file their yearly state taxes. Although the budget process took much longer than it needed to, Democrats were proud to deliver a budget that provides this tax credit that will put money back into people's pockets. Senator Hughes explained, "Most notably, we delivered on affordability. This budget includes a new tax credit that will impact almost one million Pennsylvanians. We've seen costs go up across the board and yet our federal government chooses to deny the affordability crisis Pennsylvanians and Americans are facing. This tax credit will provide some relief to hard working people who are getting crushed by high costs. The fight was long, but Senator Hughes, Governor Shapiro, and state Democrats never gave up on fighting for students, seniors, and working families.

Peter,

As a law professor, I always tell my students that it's never a good idea to procrastinate. You might think you've got it in the bag, that a last-minute push will somehow bring out your best work, or that it's really not that much to do. But trust me, procrastination almost always sets you back.

And I have to say, I think a lot of Iowans wish someone had given Mariannette Miller-Meeks that same advice.

There's no good reason to put off holding an in-person town hall until the very last minute while you're on a nearly-40-day vacation in the district. Well... actually, there _is_ a reason: **She's been ducking accountability.** When you spend your time voting against affordable healthcare and support for working families, you probably don't want to hear from the people you're supposed to represent.

It's time for something different, Peter. The truth is, the bar for representation in our district has been on the floor for a while, and I'm ready to raise it.

I want to be your representative so I can _show up_ for you and fight for what matters: Affordable healthcare, good schools, reproductive rights, and an economy that actually works for Iowans.

My team and I have been working around the clock to share that vision, but we need your help to keep up the momentum. If you're ready for leadership that doesn't wait until the last minute to do the right thing, will you chip in today toward our mid-month goal? Our deadline hits at midnight tonight >> **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cb-q4-2025?refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/119309758/582629480/-1610961223?refcode=em25_251114_MM3Pro_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_251114_MM3Pro_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=e4ceab0d-b4c1-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNGNlYWIwZC1iNGMxLWYwMTEtODE5Ni02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2zthXTcFdqvSRPAbg7fbSWqR-5AQM6-UcxTuQ5KLoo4=)**

name: Amanda Gnaedinger, LCV
subject: This is what winning looks like — victories for democracy keep rolling in at the state level
body:
See the state policy wins you helped make possible >>

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTMxODUyNTcS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjM0MDE3ODkxNAS2&mt=1&rt=0).
| | | |
---
|
* * *
---
| | | | Peter — as President Trump defies the courts and undermines our way of life, it’s clearer than ever that the future of our democracy can’t depend on action in Washington, D.C. alone. It will require a movement that is fired up in every state in our nation.
---
| | Across the country, LCV and our 30 state affiliates are standing up for fair elections, blocking voter suppression efforts, and strengthening the democratic systems that protect people and the planet.
---
| | We’re reaching out today because as an LCV supporter, we wanted to give you an update on the incredible work that YOU make possible.
---
| | [**Read more about recent state democracy victories, made possible by your support >>**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | **Here’s just a glimpse of what our state affiliates have accomplished: **
---
| |
* **Colorado** : Conservation Colorado helped pass a groundbreaking _State Voting Rights Act_ that empowers communities of color to challenge unfair election systems that prevent their voices from being heard. [**Learn more about how the** _**State Voting Rights Act**_**was passed >>**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/bxyvTVxepGH-)

---
| |
* **Michigan:** Michigan LCV led the charge to defeat a restrictive constitutional amendment that would have made it harder to register and vote. [**_Get the full scoop on this voting rights victory >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)

---
| |
* **Washington:** Washington Conservation Action hosted a statewide Democracy Lobby Day, helping expand automatic voter registration to include Tribal entities and the state health authority. [**_Read more about Washington’s Democracy Lobby Day and other state events >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)

---
| |
* **Virginia:** Virginia LCV helped advance a restoration of rights amendment to the state constitution, moving the state closer to restoring voting rights for previously incarcerated Virginians re-entering society. [**_Read more about the effort to restore voting rights to previously incarcerated individuals >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)

---
| |
---
| | _Washington Conservation Action team members and partners at the state capitol building for Democracy Lobby Day on February 12, 2025. Credit: Mallori Pryse, Washington Conservation Action_
---
| | | [ READ MORE >> ](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~NwYf4m~)
---
| | Each of these policy victories strengthens the foundation of our democracy — and with it, our ability to fight for clean air, safe drinking water, and a livable planet for everyone.
---
| | LCV and our 30 state affiliates are demonstrating what’s possible when people come together to counter authoritarianism and defend the rights of everyday people to have a say in how their government is run.
---
| | Together, we’re making sure our government reflects and protects us all. This work wouldn’t be possible without your support, Peter, and we are so grateful to you for standing by us in the critical moment for our democracy.
---
| | With hope and determination,
---
| | Amanda Gnaedinger
Senior Director, State Policy & Democracy
League of Conservation Voters
---
| | |
* * *
---

name: Tom Fitton
subject: Election Day Update!
body:
Michigan Leftists Targeted Trump

[INSIDE JW]

SUPREME COURT TO HEAR MISSISSIPPI BALLOT DEADLINE CASE

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=36489&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj13LXEzWnRfejEtcyZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=7145a213cba09a47da9a1f3ddd3d0872ca358f0a100342deb0ec461533183977]

The U.S. Supreme Court has granted review
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=36456&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc3VwcmVtZWNvdXJ0Lmdvdi9vcmRlcnMvY291cnRvcmRlcnMvMTExMDI1em9yX2JxbWMucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=03aefe3e9085cc48c969fb5ddc47de14f83488ba54ae928a324fb96d9cf08f46]
of our landmark election integrity case on behalf of the Libertarian
Party of Mississippi. We are seeking to uphold a ruling
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=34793&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdm90ZXMtYWZ0ZXItZWxlY3Rpb24tZGF5Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=c0f3568420a376267ec55d2667e6ff169135ee4f00825fb2d6696fb02eb9cfbb]
by the U.S.
Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, which struck down a
Mississippi law unconstitutionally allowing election officials to
count mail-in ballots received up to five days after Election Day.

The Supreme Court now has an opportunity to reaffirm that “Election
Day” means what it says under federal law. Counting ballots received
after Election Day not only violates federal law but encourages voter
fraud and undermines voter confidence. The Supreme Court should uphold
the historic decision by the Fifth Circuit that sensibly concluded
that counting ballots received after Election Day is unlawful.

The October 2024, Fifth Circuit appellate opinion
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=34781&F=T&&hash=9a03da0f39a326b1583d9b03b2fba14021abdf4ced5af55fc691c141b692340d]
found:

> Congress statutorily designated a singular “day for the
> election” of members of Congress and the appointment of
> presidential electors. Text, precedent, and historical practice
> confirm this “day for the election” is the day by which ballots
> must be both cast by voters and received by state officials. Because
> Mississippi’s statute allows ballot receipt up to five days after
> the federal election day, it is preempted by federal law. We reverse
> the district court’s contrary judgment and remand for further
> proceedings.

In August, we filed a brief
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=35857&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvc2NvdHVzLWJhbGxvdHMtYWZ0ZXItZWxlY3Rpb24tZGF5Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=8039c961bba2a9cb6c71b33c4e6d4beb3d402d9723566bbcbc1edde975f371a6]
with the Supreme Court, opposing Mississippi’s attempt to overturn
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=34793&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdm90ZXMtYWZ0ZXItZWxlY3Rpb24tZGF5Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=c0f3568420a376267ec55d2667e6ff169135ee4f00825fb2d6696fb02eb9cfbb]
the Fifth
Circuit’s October 2024 decision (_Michael Watson, Mississippi
Secretary of State v. Republican National Committee, et al._
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=36490&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21zLXYtcm5jLXNjb3R1cy1lbGVjdGlvbi1kYXktd3JpdC0yNC0xMjYwL11fLF8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=463e7f8a420020838d03938b54a7814705fe0a32c7bf4cd3d4cad432324ceca4
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=35846&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21zLXYtcm5jLXNjb3R1cy1lbGVjdGlvbi1kYXktd3JpdC0yNC0xMjYwLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=5b996bd337e1045eea41b9d6722fe5ca53e29e4aad9f09454b6e746b440f298d]
(No. 24-1260)).

Our brief recounts:

> In reversing the district court on the merits, the [Fifth Circuit]
> panel faithfully followed this Court’s precedent ... [T]his Court
> found that the Election Day statutes preempted a Louisiana law that
> allowed congressional candidates to be elected in October.... In
> interpreting the meaning of “day of the election” within the
> Election Day statutes, this Court found that “[w]hen the federal
> statutes speak of ‘the election’ of a Senator or Representative,
> they plainly refer to the combined actions of voters and officials
> meant to make a final selection of an officeholder.” ...
> Accordingly, the “day of the election” “may not be consummated
> prior to federal election day.”

We initially filed the civil rights lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=31320&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY291bnRpbmctYmFsbG90cy1hZnRlci1lbGVjdGlvbi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=30445c04db80403014cf6801c0a539109bdf148b2ee17d0c66123ba49e0dfac1]
in
February 2024 on behalf of the Libertarian Party of Mississippi,
challenging the election law. The suit was consolidated with one filed
by the Republican National Committee, the Mississippi Republican
Party, and other complainants.

This case is part of our national leadership in voting integrity and
voting rights. Our team of voting rights attorneys has stopped
discriminatory elections in Hawaii, and cleaned up voter rolls in
California, Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky, among other achievements
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=33927&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdGFnL2VsZWN0aW9uK2xhdz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=03a9e41170e615b9b89647833814b4689b78fdefa96f8deb87133aa58ad7082c].

We recently filed an _amici curiae_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=36451&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvYW1pY2ktYnJpZWYtYXNraW5nLXNjb3R1cy1hZmZpcm0tc3RhbmRpbmcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=9336b8ee13e92d319a4a3442a88ae8090759987c6f6ff53ddff4aec330a7e0eb]
(friends of the court) brief along with the Allied Educational
Foundation (AEF) to the Supreme Court of the United States, asking the
court to reverse the Third Circuit’s decision
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77739&L=36425&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9jYXNlcy5qdXN0aWEuY29tL2ZlZGVyYWwvYXBwZWxsYXRlLWNvdXJ0cy9jYTMvMjMtMTU5MC8yMy0xNTkwLTIwMjUtMDQtMjUucGRmP3RzPTE3NDU2MDA0MTEmdXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=19fcf9ecec7d0c3b65e016a352853a84bd0fb31bc28b79e2654a46ff534dbc99]
